mathematics.text: Nontriviality requires a closed representative and proof that it is not exact. The answer depends on the actual differential, degree, coefficient domain and any quotient by boundary terms.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The current export’s failed square-zero test blocks cohomology claims that rely on that specific object. Expected basis elements or a selected representative cannot substitute for cocycle and nontriviality witnesses.

terms.label: Measurement and detector
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A measurement is a procedure that produces an outcome. A detector is part of the apparatus or mathematical model that specifies how a system contributes to that outcome.
definitions.physics: A detector model provides an operational functional or measurement rule linking a state or field to an output. Response profile, calibration and noise assumptions are separate physical inputs.
definitions.mathematics: A detector can be modeled as a map from admissible data or states to a value, distribution of outcomes or other operational output. Its domain and continuity conditions must be specified.
definitions.specialist: Operational identification is a separate interface between the carrier and empirical claims. A declared detector functional fixes what the reconstruction theorem returns.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A model of a microphone needs more than a sound wave: it needs the microphone’s sensitivity and a rule connecting its response to a reading. The project asks for those connections rather than treating a field equation as a prediction by itself.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The wave benchmark uses a fixed smeared detector to define one observable. It does not construct a complete measurement apparatus or certify empirical accuracy; the fixed model isolates a reconstruction question.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: In the benchmark it is a fixed functional of the wave. Mathematical existence of its value and a computable or fast representation of that value are different assertions, even for the same map.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Keep its normalization, support, error estimates and output representation visible. A successful scalar detector theorem neither establishes a full observable algebra nor validates a noise model or experimental protocol.

terms.label: Field
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: In physics, a field assigns a quantity to locations in space and time. Temperature across a room is a familiar example; other fields have several components or describe geometry.
definitions.physics: A physical field is a spacetime-dependent scalar, vector, tensor or other geometrical quantity, possibly interpreted distributionally. Its type and admissible regularity are part of the model.
definitions.mathematics: A physical field is often a section of a bundle over spacetime, or a distributional generalization. This use is distinct from a scalar field in algebra, such as the rationals or a finite field.
definitions.specialist: Specify field content, grading, domain and carrier before comparing constructions. A scalar witness, a reduced tensor sector and the full metric gauge complex are different objects.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A field equation says how those quantities are related. To turn that equation into a problem, we still need to specify the allowed fields, their initial or boundary data and what a detector reads from them. “Field” also has an unrelated algebraic meaning.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The metric is a field in gravity, whereas a scalar wave is a different object. A finite number of mode coefficients is a representation or truncation, not automatically the full field space.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The function-space structure controls which equations and evaluations are meaningful. The atlas separates the finite algebraic carrier from continuum field-theoretic carriers; sharing arithmetic notation does not identify them.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A result about finitely many scalar modes is not a full metric-field theorem. Annotation of the bare word field is disabled because the corpus also uses its algebraic meaning; contextual phrases should select the intended entry.

terms.label: Spacetime and metric
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Spacetime combines locations and times into one geometrical setting. A metric tells us how separations are measured; in relativity it also determines which directions light can travel.
definitions.physics: A spacetime metric is a nondegenerate symmetric tensor fixing interval geometry and, in Lorentzian signature, null cones. The metric is dynamical in metric theories of gravity.
definitions.mathematics: A metric in this setting is a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form on each tangent space, varying with the base point. A Lorentzian metric is indefinite and is not a distance function in the metric-space sense.
definitions.specialist: Retain background geometry, signature and global assumptions as dependencies. Metric perturbations, scalar witness fields and induced mode pairings occupy different levels of the construction.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A diagram’s coordinates are labels, while the metric supplies geometrical information. A gravity model must specify how this geometry behaves. Changing the metric can change causal relationships, not just the appearance of a drawing.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Causal support statements depend on this geometry. An analysis performed on a fixed background or reduced sector must not be read as a construction of the full dynamical metric theory.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Additional global conditions enter evolution theorems. A local tensor identity alone does not supply the global causal or analytic hypotheses needed for a Green operator.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The programme’s failed full-export prerequisite is an algebraic consistency issue for a particular encoded object. It must not be confused with a general refutation of the underlying spacetime geometry or classical BRST architecture.

terms.label: Wave equation
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A wave equation relates changes in time to changes across space, describing how a disturbance evolves. Familiar examples model vibrations of strings or the travel of sound.
definitions.physics: The wave equation is a hyperbolic evolution equation whose precise form depends on the background and field type. Initial data and the chosen solution class determine the problem.
definitions.mathematics: A standard scalar form is ∂²_t u−c²Δu=0. More general geometries use the appropriate wave operator, and weak or distributional solutions require a declared testing convention.
definitions.specialist: The finite chiral fixtures give exact wave residuals within their declared arithmetic and mode family. WR and WRμ add a specific observable-reconstruction obligation.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: The equation alone does not select one wave: starting data and boundary conditions matter. The project uses a deliberately fixed wave and detector to ask how much information is needed to reconstruct a reading from approximations.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The benchmark fixes the physical evolution while changing whether approximation data include a convergence rate. Exact satisfaction by finite modes does not establish localization, a completed energy carrier or a full gauge-field propagator.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Existence, uniqueness and regularity depend on domains and data spaces. The reverse-mathematical statement concerns a particular coded solution and detector task; it is not a classification of every wave-equation theorem.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The reversal already operates at fixed time and profile, locating the additional logical cost in amplitude completion. No full Lorentzian metric BV propagator or causal quantum construction follows from this scalar benchmark.

terms.label: Mode and amplitude
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A mode is a chosen building-block pattern; its amplitude says how much of that pattern is present. Combining modes with different amplitudes can describe a more complicated wave.
definitions.physics: A mode decomposition expresses a field in a chosen family of profiles with scalar or vector coefficients. The coefficients are amplitudes; the basis and normalization determine their meaning.
definitions.mathematics: Modes are elements of a specified spanning or spectral family, and amplitudes are their coefficients. Infinite expansions require a topology and convergence statement beyond formal linear combination.
definitions.specialist: Keep the labelled finite mode set, normalization and coefficient domain in the certificate. A reduced-mode result has a different scope from the full field complex.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A musical sound can be described by several tones and their strengths. Having only finitely many tones makes one model finite, but a limit involving infinitely many still needs a convergence rule. The amplitudes contain information, not just decoration on the equation.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A finite truncation keeps selected coefficients. In the wave reversal, a single amplitude carries the limiting information while the profile and detector remain fixed. The result therefore does not depend on complicated mode mixing.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Different notions of basis have different reconstruction properties. The finite fixtures avoid those issues by declaring a labelled finite family; completion and representation questions enter only at additional stages.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The amplitude encoding used by WR is a logical reduction within a fixed physical profile. It is neither a particle-state construction nor a claim that arbitrary full-field data have a certified mode expansion.

terms.label: Energy
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Energy is a quantity a physical model uses to describe such things as motion, deformation and interactions. Its formula depends on the model. “Finite energy” says that this quantity does not diverge for the object being considered.
definitions.physics: Energy is a model-dependent quantity associated, where applicable, with time evolution and time-translation symmetry. An energy functional may also define or control a useful norm.
definitions.mathematics: An energy is a specified functional on the admissible data or solution space. Finiteness, nonnegativity, conservation and coercivity are distinct properties that need their own hypotheses.
definitions.specialist: Read the ladder’s exact positive finite energy as a fixture-level certificate. Its boundary excludes completion and causal or spatial support unless separately established.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A wave can have finite energy without being confined to a small region. Also, a finite number is not necessarily positive. The site keeps finite energy, positive energy and acceptable quantum probabilities as separate questions.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A finite-mode computation can establish an exact positive finite energy for its fixture. That is not a theorem about the completed carrier, causal support or the positivity of a quantum state on a full observable algebra.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A positive quadratic energy may induce a norm after handling null directions; an indefinite form does not. Extending the functional to a completion requires suitable control and cannot be inferred from its finite-dimensional formula alone.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Do not substitute an energy bound for a positive state, a BRST-compatible pairing or a unitarity theorem. The reduced cutoff obstruction addresses a different acceptance condition even when both calculations use the same mode language.

terms.label: Positive energy
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Positive energy means that the specified energy quantity is nonnegative, or strictly positive where the statement says so. It is a property of that energy formula and the objects to which it applies.
definitions.physics: Positive energy is an energy-functional or spectral condition, depending on the claim. The allowed configurations and the treatment of zero modes must be stated.
definitions.mathematics: A positive quadratic energy may mean E(x)>0 for every nonzero admissible x; a nonnegative energy allows a kernel. A lower-bounded operator spectrum is a related but different formulation.
definitions.specialist: The finite chiral certificate’s positive energy does not discharge the quantum probability obligation. Retain its finite fixture and normalization rather than promoting it to a physical-state theorem.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: This is different from saying that every possible measurement has a sensible probability. The project can verify positive energy for a finite wave fixture while still leaving the full quantum state problem open.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A lower energy bound does not establish positivity of the state functional or absence of problematic gauge-sector directions. Conversely, a positive quantum state need not have a Hamiltonian bounded below. These tests answer different physical questions.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Specify which definition is used, together with the domain and null directions. Finite-dimensional positivity of a matrix does not by itself prove a corresponding property on an infinite completed carrier.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: When diagnosing higher-derivative modes, separate energy sign, inner-product sign, gauge triviality and nonlinear continuation. A finding in one of those tests does not decide the others.

terms.label: Causality and causal support
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Causality restricts which events can influence which others. Causal support says that a response occurs only in the region allowed by the chosen spacetime’s causal geometry.
definitions.physics: Causal support is a support inclusion determined by the Lorentzian geometry, such as a retarded response lying in the causal future of its source. The precise domain and global assumptions matter.
definitions.mathematics: Causal constructions combine differential equations with geometric support conditions. A right or left inverse of an operator is not automatically its advanced or retarded Green operator.
definitions.specialist: LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL is a dependency tag, not automatic certification. The full off-shell metric propagator and renormalized time-ordered products remain unestablished absent their explicit certificates.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A retarded response to a source must not appear before the source can affect it. Solving an equation algebraically does not prove this restriction; the solution’s location in space and time must also be checked.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A Euclidean inverse, a finite-mode propagator or an algebraic identity does not establish this property for the full metric complex. The programme records Lorentzian causal construction as an independent obligation.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A theorem must specify the source and target spaces, operator identities and causal support inclusion. Chain-map identities and continuity may be additional requirements; none should be silently substituted for the others.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The scoped hyperbolicity witnesses rule out tested architectures rather than every possible causal construction. Local algebraic or reduced-mode progress cannot be promoted across this boundary by using causal terminology.

terms.label: Locality and spatial localization
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Locality concerns how a law relates nearby places or events. Spatial localization concerns where a particular object is concentrated or can be nonzero. They are related questions, but not the same property.
definitions.physics: Locality may refer to local differential dynamics or, in a quantum setting, specified compatibility at spacelike separation. Localization refers to support or concentration of data, fields or states.
definitions.mathematics: Spatial support is a property of a function or distribution. Locality of an operator typically restricts dependence on its input near a point; quantum locality is formulated through algebraic relations and causal regions.
definitions.specialist: Keep local BRST cohomology, localized configurations and Lorentzian causal products distinct. The adjective local does not identify their result types.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A differential equation can be local while one of its sinusoidal solutions extends across all space. Keeping only a finite list of such waves does not automatically create a disturbance confined to a small region.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Each use needs a precise statement. The finite chiral construction establishes an equation and energy within its family but does not certify spatial localization or a local observable algebra.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A support theorem, an operator-locality statement and a commutation condition are different assertions. The intended topology and the meaning of concentration must also be specified when exact support is not claimed.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Finite mode truncations can lose locality even when the original differential expression is local. Any interface used to transfer a locality or support claim needs its own preservation argument.

terms.label: Initial-value problem
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: An initial-value problem asks how a system evolves from specified starting information. The equation supplies a rule of change, while the initial data select the situation being evolved.
definitions.physics: An initial-value problem combines evolution equations, a starting hypersurface and admissible data, with any constraints imposed by the model. Different equation orders require different data structures.
definitions.mathematics: An initial-value formulation specifies an operator, data traces and a solution space. A well-posedness statement usually includes existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence in declared topologies.
definitions.specialist: The programme’s hyperbolicity no-go results concern specified witness architectures and parameter families. They do not rule out every possible formulation of the classical initial-value problem.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For a vibrating string, its initial shape alone is usually insufficient: its initial velocity matters too. The required amount and regularity of starting information depend on the equation and the allowed class of solutions.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Existence, uniqueness and stable dependence are separate acceptance questions. A normally hyperbolic scalar witness or a finite mode evolution is not the full constrained initial-value theory for metric gauge fields.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Gauge equations can require compatibility conditions or equivalence classes rather than unrestricted data. Finite exact evolution does not supply the estimates needed for an infinite-dimensional formulation.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Keep principal-operator properties, gauge-complex identities and global causal construction separate. The failed full-export identity blocks its dependent transfer irrespective of whether a reduced scalar evolution can be solved.

terms.label: Lorentzian and Euclidean signature
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Lorentzian geometry distinguishes time directions from space directions and supports light cones. Euclidean geometry uses a positive metric with no corresponding distinction. Calculations in the two settings answer different questions.
definitions.physics: Lorentzian signature is indefinite with one time direction in the usual spacetime setting; Euclidean signature is positive definite. Their evolution, spectral and state constructions use different analytic structures.
definitions.mathematics: Signature records the numbers of positive and negative directions of a nondegenerate symmetric form. Lorentzian and positive-definite metrics induce different operator and geometric problems.
definitions.specialist: EUCLIDEAN-SPECTRAL and LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL mark different dependency classes. Neither label is a confidence score, and the former cannot certify the latter’s obligations.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A Euclidean calculation may be a useful way to study a theory. It does not automatically describe how a physical disturbance travels through time. A justified connection to the Lorentzian problem is an additional step.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Analytic continuation or reconstruction requires hypotheses and compatible data. A Euclidean determinant or stability estimate does not by itself construct a BRST-compatible Hadamard state or Lorentzian time-ordered products.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Elliptic spectral control and hyperbolic causal control are distinct. A formal substitution of a time coordinate is not a proof that distributions, domains or positivity conditions transfer between the two settings.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The Euclidean stability counterfamily is scoped to its proposed estimate. Its failure does not refute every reconstruction programme, just as a successful spectral calculation would not establish the full Lorentzian quantum master equation.

terms.label: Symmetry
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A symmetry is a transformation that preserves some specified feature of a model, such as its equations or predictions. The feature being preserved must be named.
definitions.physics: A symmetry acts on fields or states while preserving the declared dynamics or observables. Global symmetries, spacetime symmetries and gauge redundancies need different treatment.
definitions.mathematics: A symmetry can be described by a group action or other transformation structure preserving specified data. Preservation of a set, equation, pairing or measure are distinct conditions.
definitions.specialist: Symmetry assumptions belong among the physical premises, while their encoded differential identities are mathematical obligations. Keep classical invariance, local anomaly classification and quantum identity restoration separate.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Turning an experiment without changing its outcome can express rotational symmetry. A change of mathematical description that represents the same physical situation is a gauge redundancy, a more specific idea explained separately.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A symmetry of a classical action may face a separate quantum consistency question. Its preservation in one truncation or sector does not establish preservation by the full interacting construction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: An isomorphism of underlying spaces need not preserve every structure of the model. State which operations and equivalences are retained before interpreting the transformation as a physical symmetry.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The presence of a BRST-style formula does not certify nilpotency of its serialized implementation. Nor does a surviving cohomology class automatically establish a symmetry-preserving physical state.

terms.label: Gauge symmetry
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Gauge symmetry describes different mathematical descriptions of the same physical situation. It tells us that some changes in the variables should not count as changes in what is physically observed.
definitions.physics: Gauge symmetry organizes redundancies of field descriptions. Gauge fixing, constraints and BRST methods address that redundancy, but their precise admissible spaces matter.
definitions.mathematics: Gauge reduction identifies configurations under a specified equivalence, often encoded infinitesimally by a complex. The quotient and any cohomological replacement depend on the actual maps and domains.
definitions.specialist: The programme separates classical directions, gauge reduction, nonlinear continuation and positive quantum interpretation. None of these stages may implicitly stand for the others.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A coordinate description can contain information that no detector distinguishes. Removing that redundancy requires a rule; simply deleting an unwanted solution is not enough to show that it was redundant.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: An extra solution direction must be tested for gauge triviality rather than assumed unphysical. Even a direction surviving that test still needs nonlinear and quantum interpretation checks before it is called a physical particle.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The square-zero condition is required before the usual cohomology is defined. Compatibility with pairings, support and boundary structures is additional data, not a consequence of taking a formal quotient.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The certified residual classes are centered deformation/vertex classes. The current serialized full complex’s consistency failure blocks its advertised transfer, without constituting a general no-go theorem for gauge symmetry or the classical programme.

terms.label: Action and Lagrangian
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: An action assigns a number to a possible history of a system. A Lagrangian supplies the local ingredients used to build that number. Requiring the action not to change to first order under allowed variations produces equations of motion.
definitions.physics: An action functional is usually an integral of a Lagrangian density, together with any boundary terms. Its stationary variations produce Euler–Lagrange equations under stated boundary conditions.
definitions.mathematics: A Lagrangian density depends on fields and specified derivatives; integration gives a functional whose first variation defines the equations and boundary contributions. The function space and variation class matter.
definitions.specialist: The pure-Weyl action is the starting point of a multi-stage construction, not its completion. Keep local variational identities, the encoded classical complex and quantum counterterm classification in their own result kinds.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: This is a compact way to specify dynamics, but it does not solve the equations or tell us which states and measurements are physically acceptable. Boundary conditions also affect which variations are allowed.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Gauge symmetry and higher derivatives can introduce constraints and additional boundary data. A formally invariant action does not establish causal well-posedness, positivity or quantum consistency.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Formal integration by parts requires the appropriate boundary or support assumptions. Local densities, integrated functionals modulo boundary terms and residual classes are distinct mathematical objects in the programme.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: No quantum coefficient or determinant should be substituted for a BV master-equation breaking. The classical import gate remains authoritative for any subsequent quantum use of transferred data.

terms.label: Weyl gravity
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Weyl gravity is a proposed theory of gravity built from a part of spacetime curvature called the Weyl tensor. Its four-dimensional pure form has a local rescaling symmetry and equations involving higher derivatives.
definitions.physics: Four-dimensional pure Weyl gravity uses a Weyl-curvature-squared action, with conformal gauge symmetry and fourth-order metric equations. It is a specific realization within the wider discussion of conformal gravity.
definitions.mathematics: The model is a metric variational theory based on a curvature-squared functional. Its gauge and differential structures require specifying the dimension, allowed metrics, boundary conditions and treatment of conformal transformations.
definitions.specialist: Pure-Weyl is the programme’s originating model; it is not an umbrella certificate for its classical, local quantum, reduced-mode and empirical results. Those dependencies remain separately tagged.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: An elegant action does not settle whether the theory supplies sensible states, causal predictions and agreement with data. Those are separate questions in this project, and the current work does not claim a complete accepted theory of nature.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Extra classical directions, gauge reduction, interactions and quantum probabilities require separate tests. The present full-export failure also means older affirmative statements about a complete BRST–Hadamard transfer must be read with the current correction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The associated complexes and residual classes are mathematical constructions with scoped claims. Their existence does not automatically furnish a positive Hilbert state space or a globally causal quantum theory.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The ruled-out hyperbolic witness architectures are scoped no-go results. The certified W₊² and W₋² residual classes are centered deformation/vertex classes, while full Lorentzian state and quantum-master-equation constructions remain unestablished without explicit certificates.

terms.label: Perturbation and linearization
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A perturbation is a change from a chosen reference situation. Linearization keeps only the part proportional to a small change, giving a simpler first approximation.
definitions.physics: Perturbation theory expands about a background, while linearization retains first-order field equations or variations. The expansion parameter and admissible background are part of the setup.
definitions.mathematics: Linearization is the derivative of an equation or map at a chosen background, on specified domain and target spaces. A kernel vector gives a formal infinitesimal solution direction.
definitions.specialist: The project distinguishes local directions, gauge reduction and nonlinear continuation before physical interpretation. Keep the expansion order and background in the certificate’s scope.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A straight line can approximate a curved graph near one point, but it need not describe the whole curve. Similarly, a solution of the linearized equations may fail to extend to a solution of the full nonlinear equations.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Linear modes help identify candidate directions and propagators. Their gauge status, nonlinear continuation and quantum positivity remain separate questions; a positive free block does not decide the interacting theory.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Integrability of that direction into a nearby family of exact solutions needs additional conditions. Higher-order obstructions, regularity and constraints cannot be inferred from the linear kernel alone.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A surviving linear or residual direction is not automatically a one-particle graviton. Finite exact perturbative checks also do not certify the full repaired complex or renormalized Lorentzian interactions.

terms.label: Free and interacting theory
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A free theory describes systems without the interactions under study; an interacting theory includes couplings that let components affect one another. Solving the free problem is often a starting point.
definitions.physics: A free theory is typically governed by a quadratic action, while interactions introduce higher-order couplings. The split depends on the chosen background and perturbative setup.
definitions.mathematics: The free/interacting distinction separates a linear or quadratic reference problem from nonlinear terms. Formal power-series solutions and convergent solutions are different mathematical claims.
definitions.specialist: Classify local counterterms and anomalies before computing coefficients, restore the local quantum master equation before residual transfer, and keep the Lorentzian gate independent.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Separate musical tones may be easy to describe, while a nonlinear coupling mixes them. A consistency test passed by isolated components need not remain true after coupling, so the project tests those stages separately.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A free propagator or positive sector does not supply renormalized time-ordered products, an interacting state or a restored quantum identity. Each requires compatible additional construction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A perturbative coefficient can satisfy a local identity without establishing a global solution or an actual measure. The relevant algebra, topology, domains and order of approximation must remain explicit.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A REDUCED-MODE or EUCLIDEAN-SPECTRAL calculation does not certify interacting causal products. Lifecycle states must record which step is complete rather than letting the word quantum imply the entire chain.

terms.label: Quantum field theory
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Quantum field theory, abbreviated QFT, combines fields with quantum rules for states, observables and probabilities. It aims to describe what measurements of fields can yield, not just a classical wave evolving in time.
definitions.physics: Quantum field theory specifies field observables, states and quantum dynamics, with further locality and covariance requirements depending on the framework. A Lagrangian is an input rather than a complete construction.
definitions.mathematics: A quantum field theory needs mathematical objects representing observables and states together with dynamics and the intended spacetime structure. Hilbert-space, algebraic and perturbative formulations organize those objects differently.
definitions.specialist: The programme has local quantum and reduced calculations, not a certified complete Lorentzian quantum theory of the full metric complex. Dependency tags constrain the use of each result.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Writing a classical field equation is therefore only one ingredient. A quantum model still needs acceptable states, a probability rule and compatible dynamics, including the treatment of interactions when they are claimed.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Finite mode models can illuminate particular obstructions, but they do not automatically define the continuum theory. Gauge redundancy, state positivity and renormalized interactions may each require their own acceptance tests.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Existence in one framework or restricted sector does not supply an equivalence with another. The atlas records carriers and obligations precisely to avoid identifying constructions solely because they use the same theory name.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A determinant, beta function, trace anomaly, local BV breaking and physical state are distinct objects. Neither a coefficient nor a residual vertex class can substitute for the missing causal and positive-state constructions.

terms.label: Quantization
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Quantization is the attempt to build a quantum description from classical starting data. It adds rules for observables, states and their probabilities rather than merely making numbers more precise.
definitions.physics: Quantization constructs quantum observables and states from a classical model under specified conventions. Gauge symmetry, operator ordering, representations and interactions can introduce additional requirements.
definitions.mathematics: Quantization can refer to several constructions, such as an operator representation, deformation of an observable algebra or a perturbative assignment. The chosen target category and correspondence conditions must be stated.
definitions.specialist: For this programme, certified classical data enter through the import gate before local quantum work is transferred. Classification, coefficient computation, QME restoration and residual transfer are separate lifecycle states.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: There can be choices and obstructions along the way. A formal recipe may produce useful equations without establishing that all its probabilities are nonnegative or that its full dynamics is well defined.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Canonical commutators or a path-integral expression are not alone a complete existence theorem. The programme separates local quantum identities, reduced sectors and full Lorentzian construction rather than treating any one as completion of quantization.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Formal algebraic existence differs from a positive representation on a Hilbert space or a measure-theoretic construction. A bridge between those objects needs its own proof and may require stronger assumptions.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: None supplies LORENTZIAN_CERTIFIED implicitly. A reduced-mode quantization is evidence for its declared sector, not for the full off-shell propagator, compatible Hadamard state or renormalized Lorentzian products.

terms.label: Particle and one-particle state
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A particle is a physical interpretation within a theory, not simply any mathematical solution. A one-particle state represents a single excitation in a setting where that distinction is meaningful. A graviton is a proposed quantum excitation of gravity.
definitions.physics: A one-particle sector is defined relative to suitable dynamics, state and representation data. On general curved backgrounds there need not be a unique preferred particle interpretation.
definitions.mathematics: A particle interpretation often uses a Hilbert representation and a decomposition of excitations relative to a reference state or symmetry. It is not an intrinsic meaning of an arbitrary cohomology group.
definitions.specialist: The certified residual W₊² and W₋² classes are centered deformation/vertex classes, not one-particle graviton states. Their nontriviality does not establish a physical spectrum.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A wave pattern or a surviving algebraic class may be a candidate ingredient, but more structure is needed to assign probabilities and identify the excitation. The project’s residual deformation classes must not be renamed gravitons on that basis alone.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Gauge reduction and linear mode counting do not themselves establish positive one-particle norms or an interacting spectrum. The programme treats existence, redundancy, nonlinear continuation and probability as different tests.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A class can instead parameterize a deformation or local interaction. Before identifying cohomology with states, specify the relevant degree, carrier, pairing and map into the physical representation.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The absence of a certified full positive Lorentzian state blocks stronger interpretations that depend on it. Scoped no-go results for propagator witnesses also do not, by themselves, prove the absence of all particle sectors.

terms.label: Ghost
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Ghost is an overloaded physics word. It can mean an auxiliary field used to account for redundant descriptions, or a problematic mode associated with signs that obstruct a physical interpretation.
definitions.physics: BRST ghosts—named within the Becchi–Rouet–Stora–Tyutin formalism—encode gauge redundancy and are not ordinarily interpreted as physical external particles. Higher-derivative ghost terminology can instead concern energy or norm signs.
definitions.mathematics: Ghost variables belong to a graded gauge construction with specified degree and statistics. This algebraic role is distinct from an indefinite bilinear form or an unstable direction of an energy functional.
definitions.specialist: Use the term with an explicit sense and result type. The trace/ghost repair concerns diagnosed components of a serialized complex, not a proof that all problematic physical modes have disappeared.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: These are not the same diagnosis. Before deciding that a ghost is harmless or fatal, ask which object is meant: a bookkeeping variable, an extra classical solution, an energy-sign problem or a negative-probability concern.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: An extra mode must be tested separately for gauge triviality, nonlinear continuation and positive quantum interpretation. A classical extra direction does not automatically prove a negative-probability state.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Cohomological reduction can remove exact directions only after the differential is valid. The physical meaning of surviving classes requires additional structure; the word ghost alone identifies neither the complex nor its interpretation.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The programme’s four tests—classical direction, gauge reduction, nonlinear continuation and state positivity—must not be collapsed into a single ghost verdict. Full repair and physical-spectrum claims remain separately gated.

terms.label: Positivity of a state
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Positivity of a quantum state is the condition that quantities representing squared measurement amplitudes receive nonnegative values. It is part of making probabilities sensible.
definitions.physics: On a unital star algebra, a state is normalized and positive: its value on A* A is nonnegative for every admissible A. In represented settings this supports the usual nonnegative probability interpretation.
definitions.mathematics: Positivity of a linear functional ω means ω(A* A)≥0; normalization is ω(1)=1 in the unital setting. The star operation, algebra and domain are part of the definition.
definitions.specialist: The reduced tensor cutoff result separates finite positive repairs from a single smooth repair preserving the stated commutator across the full declared mode family. Its conclusion is scoped to that reduced reference.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: This is different from positive energy. It is also a condition on all the relevant observables, not just a few finite tests. The cutoff example shows why passing every separately repaired finite model can still leave the required full construction impossible under its assumptions.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A candidate two-point function must satisfy the relevant positivity and compatibility conditions. Preserving a commutator or satisfying a field equation is not sufficient. Gauge descriptions may require a physical reduction before this interpretation is available.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The matrix restrictions induced by finite observable families are necessary checks. A family of independently chosen positive restrictions is not automatically the restriction of one compatible full state with the required regularity.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: It does not decide full strict-386 physical positivity or construct a compatible metric BV state. Record the reference, regularity and compatibility conditions before transporting either a positive example or an obstruction.

terms.label: Born rule
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: The Born rule is the quantum rule connecting a state to probabilities of measurement outcomes. In a simple state-vector description, probabilities come from squared amplitudes.
definitions.physics: For a normalized state and a projective measurement, the Born rule assigns an outcome probability from the corresponding projection’s expectation value. More general measurements use positive effects summing to the identity.
definitions.mathematics: In a Hilbert representation, a normalized vector ψ assigns a projection E the value ⟨ψ,Eψ⟩. A density operator ρ gives Tr(ρE); algebraic states evaluate admissible measurement effects.
definitions.specialist: The probability obligation is distinct from spectral reality, gauge-complex consistency and local quantum identity restoration. A residual class does not already define a Born-rule state.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Squaring an amplitude is only meaningful after specifying the state, measurement and normalization. A model with equations but no acceptable probability assignment has not yet supplied the predictions this rule is meant to describe.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Positivity and normalization are essential, and the observable representation must be specified. Real frequencies or positive classical energy alone do not supply those ingredients.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The Hilbert inner product or positive functional is structural data, not notation that can be attached to an arbitrary indefinite pairing. The model must also identify which effects represent the intended measurements.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: When comparing carriers, verify that the operational identification and positive normalization are preserved. An algebraic correspondence alone cannot justify transporting empirical probabilities.

terms.label: Unitarity
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Unitary evolution preserves the inner-product structure used to compare quantum state vectors. In the usual positive Hilbert setting, this preserves their normalization and the total probability.
definitions.physics: A unitary operator U on a Hilbert space satisfies U*U=UU*=1. Unitary dynamics or a unitary scattering operator must be established on the declared physical space.
definitions.mathematics: Unitarity is an inner-product-preserving surjective linear isomorphism in the complex Hilbert setting. For continuous time evolution, generator and domain conditions enter the construction of a unitary group.
definitions.specialist: The programme treats unitarity as a physical obligation independent of local BRST identities, finite positive blocks and Euclidean spectral calculations. Specify whether the claim concerns evolution or scattering.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: The meaning depends on having the right state space. A calculation with real frequencies or a formally norm-preserving matrix is not by itself a complete argument that a gauge theory has sensible physical probabilities.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: An indefinite metric introduces a different preservation condition and does not automatically give ordinary probability conservation. Free-sector results also need not extend to interactions or the full gauge-reduced model.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A symmetric formal differential expression is not automatically self-adjoint, and spectral reality alone is not an existence theorem for the desired dynamics. The carrier and domains cannot be suppressed.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: No full interacting Lorentzian unitarity conclusion follows from the reduced cutoff analysis or certified residual vertex classes. A scoped failure of one stability shortcut likewise does not settle all possible unitarity constructions.

terms.label: Cutoff and truncation
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A cutoff limits which parts of a model are included. A truncation keeps a finite or otherwise restricted part, such as only the first several wave modes.
definitions.physics: A cutoff restricts momenta, modes, volume or another declared feature. Its removal requires appropriate convergence, compatibility and sometimes renormalization conditions.
definitions.mathematics: Truncation produces a restricted family of problems indexed by a bound. Passing from solutions at every finite index to one full solution exchanges quantifiers and requires a compatibility or compactness argument.
definitions.specialist: Keep the cutoff parameter, restricted sector, reference pairing and correction class explicit. The reduced result rules out a smooth full repair under its commutator constraint, not every possible full theory.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: This can make a calculation manageable. But an answer that works for each cutoff separately need not produce one answer that remains compatible as the cutoff is removed. The project uses that difference as a central example.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: For the reduced positivity example, each finite mode set can admit a repair, while no single smooth repair satisfies the full stated constraints. That is a scoped full-family obstruction, not a claim that every finite approximation is useless.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A nested sequence of finite spaces supplies organization, not automatically convergence of solutions or preservation of positivity. The topology and uniform estimates determine which limiting conclusions are justified.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Finite exact verification establishes the stated fixture properties. It cannot be promoted to completion, causal support or an infinite state theorem merely because all sampled cutoffs pass.

terms.label: Continuum limit
terms.scope: Physical meaning, mathematical requirements and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A continuum limit is a proposed passage from discrete or truncated descriptions to a model with continuously varying space, time or unrestricted field data. It requires a rule saying how the approximations approach the intended object.
definitions.physics: A continuum limit removes a discretization or regulator in a declared sense, often while adjusting parameters or controlling observables. Mode completion and lattice-spacing limits are related examples with different details.
definitions.mathematics: A limiting construction requires objects, comparison maps and a convergence notion or universal property. Completing a normed space and taking a regulator-removal limit are not identical operations.
definitions.specialist: The atlas separates finite carriers from continuum and local field-theoretic carriers. A finite witness or detector reconstruction does not cover every interface needed to reach the latter.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Making a grid finer or adding more modes is not itself proof that predictions settle. The quantities being compared, their error controls and the properties required of the limit all have to be specified.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Convergence of one observable does not establish locality, all correlations or a positive full state. The required topology and compatibility conditions depend on the claimed physical construction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Existence at each finite stage is weaker than existence of compatible limiting data. Uniform estimates, compactness or explicit construction can supply bridges, but each introduces assumptions that must be recorded.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Retain exact versus numerical result types and the declared observable scope. The reduced positivity obstruction demonstrates a specific failure of full regularity despite finite repairability; it is not a universal continuum no-go theorem.

terms.label: Reverse foundations of physics
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: Reverse foundations of physics starts with a job a theory must do—such as predicting a detector reading—and asks what physical ideas and mathematical assumptions make that job possible.
definitions.physics: The programme decomposes a physical theory into postulates, carriers, logical existence assumptions, operational identifications and empirical protocols. It asks which combinations support a specified obligation.
definitions.mathematics: Reverse foundations is an organizational programme comparing the structures and assumptions used to discharge physical obligations. It includes representation-sensitive existence questions alongside algebraic, analytic and empirical ones.
definitions.specialist: The current synthesis organizes scoped implications without claiming a finished theory or universally formalized audit framework. The wave reversal and reduced positivity obstruction isolate different dependency failures.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: This reverses the usual presentation that starts with an impressive equation and moves forward. It encourages a reader to ask where states, probabilities, limits and observations enter, and to notice when a necessary connection has not been supplied.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: This is broader than reverse mathematics, which calibrates logical strength over a base. A carrier comparison or empirical failure can be informative without being a reverse-mathematical equivalence.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The atlas is a coordinate system for those questions, not a single metatheorem that every cell has been mechanically proved. Interfaces between separately established results need explicit preservation conditions.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Preserve the distinction between logical calibration, carrier construction, physical interpretation and empirical acceptance. A theory profile with many populated cells is not a compatible end-to-end realization of their claims.

terms.label: Physical postulate
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: A physical postulate is an assumption about how the modeled world behaves. It can concern interactions, symmetries or what counts as an observable. It is different from a mathematical rule used to reason about that model.
definitions.physics: Physical postulates specify modeled properties such as locality, covariance or conformal symmetry. Their encoding in a carrier is another input, alongside the logical principles used in proofs.
definitions.mathematics: A physical premise becomes usable in mathematics through an explicit encoding as conditions on objects and maps. The encoding is not supplied by the proposition’s informal physical name.
definitions.specialist: Keep physical premises separate from logical axioms, carrier structure and empirical protocols in every obligation claim. Their encoded form and normalization are part of the provenance.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For example, assuming that influences obey a causal restriction is a physical choice. A theorem may show what follows from that choice, but the theorem alone does not show that the choice matches nature.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The same verbal postulate can admit inequivalent mathematical realizations. State which realization and operational meaning are intended before comparing results or importing a theorem from another carrier.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Proof establishes consequences of those conditions. It does not establish that they capture the intended empirical situation, nor that a different encoding preserves the same observables or existence requirements.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A formal causal-looking term or symmetry label is insufficient to promote the result’s dependency tag. The corresponding construction and preservation properties must actually be certified at the scope being claimed.

terms.label: Foundational regime
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: A foundational regime is a chosen approach to which mathematical objects and reasoning principles are allowed. It is one of the organizing axes of the atlas.
definitions.physics: A foundational regime records the mathematical permission structure under which a physical obligation is studied. It is distinct from the carrier family and from the physical postulates.
definitions.mathematics: The atlas groups foundational environments for comparison, but those labels are not themselves formal theories with automatically established implications. The theorem must still identify its exact base and coding.
definitions.specialist: A regime coordinate records scope; it is not proof that a cell holds for every object or axiom system informally associated with that regime. Cell evidence remains witness- and obligation-specific.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: It is not a ladder of reader intelligence or a score for how true a physical theory is. The same physical task can be asked under several regimes to reveal which existence assumptions its answer uses.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A finite exact construction, a constructive realization and a set-theoretic existence argument may address similar physics while providing different guarantees. Compare the actual assumptions and outputs rather than only their regime labels.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Reverse-mathematical systems such as RCA₀ and ACA₀ provide precise calibrations for particular assertions. Broader constructive or set-theoretic categories require additional specification before a strength comparison is meaningful.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Composition requires compatible realizations and assumption transport. Neither neighboring coordinates nor a shared theory profile certify those interfaces or establish a global ordering of all regimes.

terms.label: Physical obligation
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: A physical obligation is a concrete job a model must perform before a claim can be trusted. Examples include defining states, evolving them, assigning probabilities and connecting an observable to data.
definitions.physics: An obligation specifies a target such as state existence, causal propagation, renormalized products or empirical acceptance. Its carrier, assumptions and success criterion must be explicit.
definitions.mathematics: An obligation is an asserted property or construction required of the declared objects. It may concern existence, uniqueness, compatibility, interpretation or an operational map.
definitions.specialist: Obligation-based reporting separates classification, coefficients, restoration, transfer and causal certification. These are not interchangeable progress labels for a single undifferentiated quantum result.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: An equation can help with some jobs while leaving others open. The project uses this checklist of mathematical and physical tasks to make progress visible without presenting a partial construction as a finished theory.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Different calculations discharge different obligations. A local quantum coefficient does not substitute for a positive state, and a fit to a bounded dataset does not establish a complete causal quantum model.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The atlas organizes sixteen such task families. A certificate for one encoded witness does not universally quantify over its carrier family unless the theorem explicitly does so; the statement and evidence must retain that distinction.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A compatible end-to-end route needs both discharged obligations and verified interfaces. Failures and missing joins should remain explicit even when other cells contain strong results.

terms.label: Atlas cell and evidence grade
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: An atlas cell is one question formed by choosing mathematical assumptions, a kind of mathematical setting and a job for a physical theory. Its evidence grade describes the kind of support recorded for that question.
definitions.physics: The atlas crosses six foundational regimes, six carrier families and sixteen obligations. Cell evidence identifies what has been constructed, bounded, ruled out or left conditional at that coordinate.
definitions.mathematics: A cell is an organizational record, not a universally quantified theorem about every object matching its row and column labels. The underlying statement, witness and assumptions determine its logical force.
definitions.specialist: Treat grades as evidence classifications with scoped provenance, not confidence scores or lifecycle promotions. Inspect dependency tags and does-not-establish fields before reusing a result.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: The 576 cells are not 576 universes. A colored cell may concern a limited example or a scoped result, and many successful cells may use incompatible constructions. Read the evidence and limits behind the color.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Coverage is not composition. A theory profile can collect results from different realizations; a theory journey must show that the states, dynamics and observables belong to one compatible route.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The table’s geometry does not supply implications between adjacent cells. Claims about transport require explicit maps and preservation conditions, independently of the grade assigned to either endpoint.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: No grid coverage count certifies the full classical import gate or a Lorentzian quantum theory. A failed prerequisite must block dependent claims even if nearby records remain valid.

terms.label: Theory journey and interface
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: A theory journey follows one proposal from assumptions through states, change, measurement and comparison with data. An interface is a justified connection between two steps.
definitions.physics: A journey tracks a compatible sequence of realizations and obligations. Interfaces specify preserved data such as observables, pairing, causal support, normalization or empirical interpretation.
definitions.mathematics: An interface is a specified map or comparison with required preservation properties. A chain map preserves differentials, but may fail to preserve pairings, topologies, support or positivity.
definitions.specialist: Interface obligations make hidden changes of carrier or claim type visible. Record the exact source object and the properties carried across each map.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Two well-built components may still fail to fit together. A state construction and a detector formula are useful only if the detector is defined on those states and retains the meaning claimed for its output.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A profile showing separate successes need not supply those interfaces. In particular, a reduced positive block and a full gauge complex are not joined merely by sharing notation or belonging to the same theory family.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Each composition theorem needs compatible domains and codomains. Abstract equivalence of underlying spaces is insufficient when the requested output includes a representation or quantitative control.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The full-export consistency failure blocks interfaces depending on that export. Valid local or reduced results survive at their own scope, but cannot be assembled into a full transfer by assuming the missing joins.

terms.label: Claim scope and assumptions
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: A claim’s scope says exactly which objects and situations it covers. Its assumptions say what must already hold for its conclusion to follow.
definitions.physics: Scope includes background, sector, data class, approximation order and target property. Assumptions include both physical premises and mathematical requirements needed by the construction.
definitions.mathematics: A statement’s force is fixed by its quantifiers, domains, hypotheses and conclusion. Coding and output requirements can materially change that statement even when the informal physical object stays the same.
definitions.specialist: Attach dependency tags and lifecycle states to the exact result kind. A does-not-establish field is a boundary, not an additional theorem or evidence for its negation.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: “This finite model works” and “every full model works” are very different claims. A precise explanation names the restrictions early so the reader does not accidentally turn a useful limited result into a statement about all of physics.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A positive reduced-mode example does not certify full-metric positivity. A failure of one hyperbolic witness family likewise does not refute every causal formulation. Preserve the quantifiers and architecture in either direction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The WR/WRμ comparison depends on this precision: a rate-free promise and a supplied modulus are different hypotheses. An abstract value and a fast name for it are different outputs.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Missing assumptions cannot be filled by adjacent certificates or plausible prose. A skipped or timed-out gate remains unresolved, and current corrections override unsupported interpretations of historical summaries.

terms.label: Certificate and provenance
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: A certificate records evidence that a specified mathematical check succeeded. Provenance records where its inputs came from and which versions were used.
definitions.physics: A computational certificate should expose the object, arithmetic, assumptions and verifier behind the result. Provenance identifies the imported source and generated inputs, usually with version and content hashes.
definitions.mathematics: A certificate is a finite witness or structured record checked against a declared predicate. A content hash identifies bytes; it does not certify the predicate’s mathematical adequacy.
definitions.specialist: The programme records source commits, schemas, hashes, assumptions, missing objects and exact commands. Classical imports remain fail-closed until every required identity gate passes.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A checksum can show that a file has not changed; it cannot show that the file describes nature correctly. The useful question is what was checked, against which assumptions, and what kinds of mistakes the check could detect.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Exact finite algebra, numerical agreement and a written infinite proof provide different evidence. A certificate for one of them cannot silently stand in for the others or for empirical validation.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The checker’s relationship to the producer matters. A successful check proves only its encoded conditions on its encoded objects, while completeness of the specification and any infinite theorem require additional justification.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Replay establishes reproduction; an independent rail addresses different failure modes. Neither can promote a local algebraic result to a Lorentzian state theorem, and a partial certificate must retain its unresolved fields.

terms.label: Independent verification
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: Independent verification checks a result by a route that does not simply repeat the same decisive assumption or calculation. Reproduction instead asks whether the original procedure gives the same answer again.
definitions.physics: An independent check targets failure modes not inherited from the producer, for example by using a distinct reduction or verifying witnesses against original operators. Reproducibility is a separate property.
definitions.mathematics: Independence is relative to the claim and possible error, not merely to program names. A verifier should check supplied witnesses or identities without assuming the conclusion it is meant to establish.
definitions.specialist: The evidence rail must distinguish reproduction, independent verification and semantic review. Shared content-addressed inputs are acceptable when their role and required checks are explicit.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Running the same program twice is useful for repeatability, but both runs can share one mistake. A separate derivation or checker can catch different errors. Neither approach eliminates the need to ask whether the right question was encoded.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Agreement between two wrappers around the same hard-coded basis is weak evidence for that basis. A useful audit exposes which mathematical data and implementation assumptions the checking routes still share.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Finite independent checks do not convert a written infinite argument into a machine-checked proof. Conversely, a formal proof still depends on the correctness and relevance of its formal statement and trusted foundation.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Do not claim independent verification by rerunning the producer or importing its expected answer. A timeout, skip or incomplete domain check leaves the relevant obligation unpassed.

terms.label: Fail-closed claim boundary
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: Fail-closed means that a claim is not accepted when a required check is missing, unfinished or unsuccessful. Silence from a check is not treated as a pass.
definitions.physics: A fail-closed gate blocks dependent use of an object until all required acceptance conditions are verified. It distinguishes an unverified construction from a refuted theory.
definitions.mathematics: A fail-closed workflow authorizes a conclusion only after its declared prerequisites have positive evidence. Unknown, timeout and skip states are not identified with truth of the required predicate.
definitions.specialist: The classical import gate requires nilpotency, contraction, chain-map, cyclicity, residual-cohomology and pairing checks for the required snapshot. Partial data cannot claim a freeze certificate.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: If a full construction needs six conditions and only five were checked, the complete claim stays open. The five successes may still be useful, but they do not fill the missing condition.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The current serialized full gravity object fails its consistency prerequisite, and a partial repair has not passed the full gate. Local or reduced results can remain valid, but cannot supply that missing acceptance by analogy.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Failure of a particular witness does not logically negate existence of every possible witness. The gate’s domain and completeness requirements therefore remain part of the result, even when the implementation reports a simple pass or fail.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Lifecycle promotion must be explicit and scoped. The repaired trace/ghost blocks do not establish full transfer, while a failed architecture does not erase unrelated certified calculations or refute the entire classical programme.

terms.label: No-go theorem and obstruction
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: A no-go theorem proves that a specified goal cannot be achieved under stated conditions. An obstruction identifies something preventing a proposed construction from working.
definitions.physics: A scoped no-go result excludes a defined class of constructions. Its architecture, parameter range, background and target requirements determine how widely the exclusion applies.
definitions.mathematics: An obstruction may be a nonvanishing class, incompatible identity or counterexample to a required estimate. A no-go conclusion requires showing that every candidate in the stated class encounters the obstruction.
definitions.specialist: Retain exact architecture and dependency tags. The 24-field scalar normally-hyperbolic witness and fixed-temporal cyclic 46-parameter first-order family are scoped exclusions.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: If one bridge design cannot span a river, that does not prove no bridge can. Likewise, a failed method can teach us which assumption or architecture must change without disproving every version of a physical theory.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The programme’s hyperbolicity witnesses exclude tested families, while the reduced positivity obstruction excludes a particular smooth full repair. Neither is a universal rejection of the classical gauge complex or all physical-state constructions.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Failure of one necessary condition for one encoded object differs from a theorem quantifying over all allowed objects. Negative conclusions must preserve those quantifiers as carefully as positive existence theorems.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The Euclidean stability counterfamily targets a proposed bound, and the current export audit targets a concrete serialized object. Do not merge those failures into an unsupported general claim about spectrum, unitarity or every Lorentzian construction.

terms.label: Finite-stage versus uniform construction
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: Solving every finite version of a problem is different from finding one solution that works for the whole unlimited problem. The separate finite solutions may disagree or become less controlled as the size grows.
definitions.physics: The distinction is between a family of finite solutions and compatible full data meeting uniform regularity or bounds. A cutoff-dependent choice may become singular or fail consistency as the cutoff grows.
definitions.mathematics: The quantifier pattern “for each N there exists x_N” does not imply “there exists x working for every N.” Even compatible approximants may need compactness or uniform estimates to yield an admissible limit.
definitions.specialist: The wave and cutoff examples expose different missing resources: convergence information for named reconstruction, and full regularity/compatibility for positivity repair. They should not be combined into one theorem.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For each short list of modes, a correction might make a positivity test pass. That does not show that one smooth correction works for all modes together. The project’s cutoff example makes this distinction concrete.

physics.heading: Use in the model
