physics.text: The reduced tensor result permits each finite positive repair but excludes one smooth repair preserving the declared commutator over the full family. It does not negate every possible choice of full carrier or physical construction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: State the topology and limiting class explicitly. Finite exact arithmetic proves the tested identities, while an infinite obstruction or completion theorem requires its own argument.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The reduced obstruction remains conditional on its reference and commutator constraints. Finite checks support the witnesses but do not certify all infinite claims, full metric positivity or causal products.

terms.label: Supplied-rate and rate-free wave reconstruction
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s claims and evidence.

definitions.general: WR names the wave-reconstruction assertion with a rate-free Cauchy input. WRμ names its supplied-rate version; μ denotes an error schedule. Both ask for a reliably approximated reading of the same fixed wave detector.
definitions.physics: The benchmark fixes the wave profile and detector while comparing rate-free Cauchy data with data carrying a modulus. WRμ is provable in RCA₀; WR is equivalent to ACA₀ over that base.
definitions.mathematics: The assertions use specified input codings and require a fast output name for the detector observable. Supplying μ allows explicit reconstruction; omitting it permits a reduction from range existence over RCA₀.
definitions.specialist: Preserve both directions and the representation boundary: RCA₀ proves WRμ, and over RCA₀ the declared WR is equivalent to ACA₀. No higher-type uniform reconstruction theorem is claimed.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: With a schedule, the input says when later approximations are accurate enough. Without one, it only promises that they eventually agree. The project proves that this difference changes the mathematical existence principles needed for the declared output.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The lower bound already occurs at fixed time and profile. It identifies amplitude completion as the additional requirement, rather than propagation, detector complexity or an empirical precision limit.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The scalar completeness reversal is standard background. The project embeds it in the fixed wave benchmark and supplies finite witnesses, while the infinite equivalence remains a written argument rather than a completed proof-assistant formalization.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The benchmark does not supply a full Lorentzian metric propagator, positive quantum state or causal interacting construction. Its contribution is a controlled comparison locating the logical cost with the physical profile and detector unchanged.

terms.label: PRA
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: PRA stands for Primitive Recursive Arithmetic. It is a mathematical rulebook for reasoning about explicitly built finite calculations and their repetitions.
definitions.physics: Primitive Recursive Arithmetic (PRA) is the stated base for each fixed finite fixture in the ladder. It formalizes the arithmetic construction rather than adding physical dynamics.
definitions.mathematics: Primitive Recursive Arithmetic (PRA) is a first-order arithmetic theory with symbols for primitive recursive functions and quantifier-free induction in a standard presentation.
definitions.specialist: Primitive Recursive Arithmetic (PRA) bounds the fixed-fixture arithmetic claims. It does not name a completed continuum field theory or supply the rate-free reconstruction principle WR.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A fixed finite wave fixture can be checked by sums, products and other prescribed arithmetic operations. This does not turn every question about infinitely many approximations into a finite calculation; the limiting task needs its own assumptions.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The certificate concerns a declared finite family and its exact identities. A uniform claim about all inputs, or passage to a completed energy carrier, has different quantifiers and must be justified separately.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Primitive recursion is a restricted way of defining total computations, not a synonym for every terminating algorithm. The formal language and the fixed-fixture quantifiers matter when comparing a PRA result with a second-order reconstruction assertion.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Keep the finite encoding and exact verification separate from an assertion about arbitrary Cauchy data. A batch of successful fixture evaluations is reproduction of those cases, not automatically the theorem uniformly quantified over them.

references.title: Simpson, Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic, Chapter I: named systems and Weak König’s Lemma

terms.label: WKL₀
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: WKL stands for Weak König’s Lemma. WKL₀ adds an infinite-path existence rule to RCA₀: a binary branching tree with arbitrarily long allowed paths has an infinite path.
definitions.physics: Weak König’s Lemma gives the additional axiom in WKL₀. The atlas uses this system to distinguish some compactness-based existence arguments from reconstruction already possible in RCA₀.
definitions.mathematics: WKL₀ is RCA₀ together with Weak König’s Lemma: every infinite subtree of the binary tree of finite zero-one strings has an infinite path.
definitions.specialist: Weak König’s Lemma is a named reference principle in the atlas, not evidence that a particular field construction has been carried out in WKL₀.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Picture successive yes-or-no choices whose allowed finite histories keep extending. The added principle guarantees a whole endless choice history. Its role here is a mathematical benchmark, not a level of physical accuracy.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: This does not make WKL₀ the stated solution of the rate-free wave task: that assertion is calibrated against ACA₀. The exact theorem, data representation and base must decide which principle is relevant.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The binary-tree restriction is essential. Neither an arbitrary branching-tree theorem nor an algorithm for choosing the path is the stated axiom. Keep WKL₀ distinct from stronger systems and from bare notational abbreviations.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Preserve the code for the tree or compactness problem and its connection to the physical obligation. The project’s WR reversal remains an ACA₀ equivalence over RCA₀; introducing this glossary entry does not alter that bound.

terms.label: ZF and choice principles
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: ZF means Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory, a standard rulebook for reasoning about sets. ZFC adds the Axiom of Choice, a further rule allowing simultaneous selections from arbitrary families of nonempty sets.
definitions.physics: Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory (ZF) specifies a foundational environment; adding Choice gives ZFC. Some state or carrier constructions can use weaker choice principles, or none, depending on their details.
definitions.mathematics: ZF stands for Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory. ZF is a set theory without the Axiom of Choice as an axiom; ZFC includes it. Countable choice, dependent choice and unrestricted choice are distinct principles.
definitions.specialist: ZF stands for Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory. Zermelo–Fraenkel (ZF) and choice-sensitive claims belong to the foundational dependency record. Do not infer their exact strength from a broad atlas regime label.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Choosing from one finite list and choosing from an unrestricted infinite family are different permissions. The project asks which selections a construction actually uses rather than automatically giving every proof all available choice rules.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A “choice-free” claim is relative to a declared formulation. It does not mean that no physical parameters were selected, and finite choices in an experiment should not be confused with a set-existence axiom.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: An explicit selection function can avoid an appeal to choice for a particular family. The precise domain and hypotheses must be retained when claiming that a construction works in ZF or requires an additional selection principle.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Carrier replacements may change which selections are needed, but require maps preserving the intended observables. A result avoiding one choice principle does not thereby establish every completion, positive-state or causal obligation for that carrier.

terms.label: Computability
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: Computability asks whether a specified procedure can produce the requested answer from the information supplied. It is different from knowing that some answer exists.
definitions.physics: Computability concerns effective access to a represented output from represented input. It is distinct from computational cost, numerical stability and experimental feasibility.
definitions.mathematics: A computability statement specifies an encoding, a class of algorithms and an input-output relation. For infinite objects, algorithms often produce names or successively refined approximations rather than one finite exact numeral.
definitions.specialist: Keep effectivity, logical strength and uniform realizability separate. WR/WRμ fixes the representation and requested fast output; its reversal is not a blanket classification of computable wave evolution.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: An error schedule can let a procedure choose an approximation at any requested accuracy. A promise that approximations eventually settle may not reveal when to stop. The input format therefore matters as much as the intended limiting object.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A detector functional can be continuous while the input lacks information needed for its demanded output name. The wave comparison isolates this issue without changing the profile or propagation, but its logical equivalence is not itself a runtime bound.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The available oracle or set parameters matter. A nonconstructive existence proof does not automatically compute the object, and a computable finite approximation need not come with a computable convergence modulus.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A finite exact implementation checks declared witnesses. It does not certify a higher-type uniform algorithm or discharge the infinite argument by testing a large finite sample.

terms.label: Uniformity
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: Uniformity means that one rule or bound works across the whole stated collection of cases. Without it, each case may need its own adjustment, with no control over how those adjustments grow.
definitions.physics: A uniform estimate bounds a specified quantity independently of the parameter being varied. The parameter might be a cutoff, time range, background or input family.
definitions.mathematics: Uniform statements keep a witness or bound independent of selected quantified variables. This changes the quantifier order relative to separate existence at each parameter value.
definitions.specialist: Specify the index set, norm or seminorm and remaining parameter dependence before claiming uniform control. Uniform operator existence is also distinct from an instance-by-instance theorem in weak foundations.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: You might repair every finite mode model separately while needing larger and larger corrections. That does not give one controlled repair of the unlimited model. The set of cases and the quantity controlled must both be named.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Uniformity in one parameter does not imply it in another. In the reduced positivity example, separate finite repairs fail the required full smoothness control; this is more specific than merely observing cutoff dependence.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A family of compatible objects may still need a compactness or convergence argument. Conversely, a uniform bound alone need not identify the desired limit or prove that all defining identities survive it.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The wave modulus comparison and reduced cutoff obstruction expose different failures of uniform access or regularity. They must not be merged into a stronger common theorem without an explicit reduction.

terms.label: Operator and domain
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: An operator is a rule acting on mathematical objects. Its domain says which inputs the rule is allowed to act on. A formula without its domain may leave the problem ambiguous.
definitions.physics: The domain is part of an operator’s physical specification, particularly for unbounded observables and generators. Boundary conditions and regularity can determine its spectrum and evolution.
definitions.mathematics: An operator is a map D(A)→Y with declared domain D(A), often a proper dense subspace of a Hilbert or Banach space. Closure and extension properties depend on that domain.
definitions.specialist: Domain compatibility is an interface obligation when passing from finite exact data to analytic carriers. Record the actual spaces, boundary conditions and extension used.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Differentiating a smooth function is straightforward; differentiating an arbitrary rough function needs a different meaning. Boundary conditions can also change the operator, even when the displayed differential formula stays the same.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A formal Hamiltonian expression does not establish self-adjointness or a unitary evolution. Likewise, a mode formula for an inverse does not fix the source and target spaces required of a causal Green operator.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Two operators can share a differential expression yet have different domains and adjoints. Formal integration by parts checks an expression-level relation, not equality with the Hilbert-space adjoint on its full domain.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Neither a chain-map certificate nor a real finite spectrum proves the needed unbounded-operator statements. Importing a spectral calculation without its domain can change the claim being transported.

terms.label: Self-adjointness
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: A self-adjoint operator is a suitably well-defined operator that equals its adjoint, the partner determined by the inner product. In infinite-dimensional spaces, this requires agreement of allowed inputs as well as formulas.
definitions.physics: Self-adjointness is A=A* with equality of domains in the relevant Hilbert space. For a generator, it supports construction of unitary time evolution under the standard hypotheses.
definitions.mathematics: A densely defined symmetric operator is self-adjoint when its domain equals that of its adjoint and their actions coincide. Essential self-adjointness means its closure is self-adjoint.
definitions.specialist: Treat self-adjointness as a domain-sensitive analytic claim. A finite exact pairing calculation does not certify it for a completed carrier or a gauge-reduced physical space.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Self-adjoint operators play an important role in quantum observables and evolution. Their eigenvalues need not all be positive, so this condition must not be confused with positive energy.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A symmetric differential expression or a finite Hermitian matrix approximation is insufficient to establish a chosen infinite operator’s self-adjointness. Boundary conditions and extensions must be specified, and a positive physical Hilbert realization is another requirement.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Symmetry alone may permit multiple extensions or no self-adjoint extension of the desired kind. Spectral conclusions attach to the actual closed operator, not merely to a formal differential expression.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: When interpreting Euclidean spectral data or Lorentzian dynamics, retain the chosen inner product and extension. Self-adjointness does not discharge state positivity, bounded-below energy and interacting causal consistency as one combined gate.

terms.label: Spectrum
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: An operator’s spectrum generalizes its possible eigenvalues. In physics it can describe frequencies or energy values associated with a specified operator and state space.
definitions.physics: The spectrum consists of values where the operator minus that value times the identity lacks the required inverse. Eigenfrequencies, Hamiltonian spectra and fluctuation-operator spectra are different uses.
definitions.mathematics: For a closed operator, the resolvent set contains parameters for which the shifted operator has the appropriate bounded inverse; its complement is the spectrum. Point spectrum is only one part.
definitions.specialist: Spectral reality, residue signs, lower energy bounds and state positivity are separate diagnostics. Retain which operator and realization a calculation addresses.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For a finite matrix, finding eigenvalues may tell the whole spectral story. Infinite systems can also have continuous spectrum. A statement that the spectrum is real does not, by itself, say that probabilities or energy are positive.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Specify the carrier and domain before applying a spectral interpretation. A spectral calculation in a Euclidean or reduced setting does not automatically identify the full Lorentzian physical particle content.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Unbounded operators require explicit domain conventions. The spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators uses a positive Hilbert structure; it cannot be applied to an arbitrary indefinite pairing by analogy.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The certified centered residual deformation classes do not constitute a one-particle spectrum. A EUCLIDEAN-SPECTRAL or REDUCED-MODE result must not be used to certify the missing full Lorentzian state construction.

terms.label: Distribution
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: In analysis, a distribution is a generalized function described by how it responds to test functions. It can represent idealized sharply concentrated sources that are not ordinary functions.
definitions.physics: Distributions let fields, sources and correlation functions be smeared against admissible tests even when pointwise values are not defined. The test space and continuity requirement specify the construction.
definitions.mathematics: A distribution is a continuous linear functional on a chosen test-function space, such as smooth compactly supported functions. Derivatives are defined by duality with the appropriate signs.
definitions.specialist: Distributional carriers introduce analytic obligations beyond finite mode identities: continuity on tests, support, singularity control and compatible operations. A formal series must be shown to define the declared distribution.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A point source can assign a test function its value at one point. That is different from a probability distribution describing uncertain outcomes. This dictionary uses the analytical meaning here and keeps automatic annotation of the bare word disabled.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A two-point distribution is not automatically a positive state, and products of singular distributions may not be defined. Regularity and wavefront conditions are important precisely because formal pointwise manipulations can fail.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Multiplication by a smooth function is well defined, whereas multiplication of two arbitrary distributions is not. Support and wavefront information refine what operations are allowed and which singularities can occur.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The ladder’s distributional stage and the full metric two-point construction are distinct targets. Neither a scalar weak solution nor a reduced reference alone certifies the latter’s positivity and gauge compatibility.

terms.label: Weak solution
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: A weak solution satisfies an equation through its responses to test functions rather than through ordinary derivatives at every point. It allows useful solutions that are too rough for the pointwise formulation.
definitions.physics: A weak formulation moves derivatives onto tests or uses a variational identity on declared spaces. It can express dynamics for finite-energy or distributional fields.
definitions.mathematics: A weak solution satisfies a specified integral or dual identity for all admissible tests. Distributional and variational formulations can be related, but equivalence depends on spaces and hypotheses.
definitions.specialist: Keep the ladder’s weak-equation statement tied to its test class and carrier. Extending finite fixtures to all tests requires the relevant continuity or density argument.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Instead of asking for a field’s value at every tiny location, one checks suitable averaged identities. This broadens the allowed solutions but does not remove the need for initial data, boundary conditions or a uniqueness argument.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The precise testing class determines the assertion. Satisfying that identity does not itself establish causal support, smoothness or the full gauge constraints; those remain separate conditions on the proposed physical solution.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Regularity theorems may upgrade a weak solution to a classical one. That upgrade is not part of the definition, and an exact finite residual check covers only the declared ansatz unless a full testing argument is supplied.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A weak scalar equation does not supply the full metric complex’s causal inverse or physical state. Imported distributional claims must retain their operator, domain, support and regularity boundaries.

terms.label: Regularity
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: Regularity describes how smooth or controlled a mathematical object is: for example, whether it has derivatives and whether those derivatives remain bounded in the required sense.
definitions.physics: Regularity specifies the differentiability or integrability class needed for fields, kernels or observables. Different norms and derivative bounds provide different controls.
definitions.mathematics: Regularity may be expressed through Cᵏ, Sobolev, distributional or microlocal conditions. Each identifies a different class; greater differentiability and control of singular directions are not interchangeable statements.
definitions.specialist: The reduced obstruction quantifies over a declared smooth correction class, not all conceivable changes of carrier, involution or commutator. Preserve those hypotheses when reusing its conclusion.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A separate finite approximation can always be smooth while the attempted infinite limit becomes singular. The required amount of smoothness is therefore an actual condition on the full construction, not a cosmetic preference.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: In the reduced positivity obstruction, the allowed correction must be one smooth kernel preserving the reference constraints. Positive repairs at each finite cutoff do not satisfy that full requirement merely because each finite repair is smooth.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Convergence in a weak topology does not imply convergence of every derivative. A limiting argument must state which seminorms are controlled uniformly and which regularity properties survive the passage to the limit.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: For the full metric complex, regularity is only one of several requirements. A Hadamard-type singularity statement cannot substitute for positive type, nilpotency or a compatible gauge descent.

terms.label: Existence, uniqueness and well-posedness
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: Existence asks whether a solution can be found. Uniqueness asks whether the permitted data select only one. Well-posedness also asks whether small changes in the data cause suitably small changes in the solution.
definitions.physics: A well-posed initial-value problem provides existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence in specified data and solution spaces. Gauge theories may formulate uniqueness only after accounting for redundancy.
definitions.mathematics: Well-posedness is a property of a specified input-output problem, not merely its differential expression. The time interval, topology and equivalence notion for solutions are essential.
definitions.specialist: Separate principal-operator criteria, complete existence estimates and the encoded complex’s consistency. The tested normally- or strongly-hyperbolic architectures are scoped witnesses, not an exhaustive classification of every formulation.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: These questions depend on which solutions are allowed. A formula that produces one example does not show that every admissible input has a unique, stable solution.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Hyperbolicity helps organize such results but is not the whole theorem. Constraints, boundary conditions and global geometry still matter, and a successful scalar formulation does not automatically establish the full metric gauge problem.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A weak existence theorem may lack uniqueness, while continuous dependence can fail in a chosen stronger topology. Logical strength may also change when the requested solution is represented with additional quantitative information.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The full-export square-zero failure blocks its dependent construction regardless of success on a reduced scalar problem. Conversely, excluding one witness family does not refute all possible well-posedness routes.

terms.label: Algebra
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: An algebra is a mathematical collection whose elements can be added and multiplied, with specified rules. For observables, multiplication helps describe combinations of quantities being studied.
definitions.physics: An observable algebra packages combinations of observables, often with an involution representing adjoints. States then assign compatible expectation values on that declared algebra.
definitions.mathematics: An algebra over a scalar field is a vector space with a bilinear multiplication satisfying the specified axioms. Associativity, a unit, commutativity and an involution are additional choices.
definitions.specialist: Keep finite exact algebras, local functional algebras and represented quantum observable algebras distinct. Their states, ideals and quotients answer different obligations.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: The rules matter: multiplying in one order may give a different result from multiplying in the reverse order. An algebra’s existence does not alone tell us which of its elements represent measurements or how probabilities are assigned.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A finite matrix algebra can model noncommuting observables exactly. Extending it to a continuum or local field algebra requires additional structure and does not follow simply by increasing the number of matrix entries.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Topological or operator algebras carry further analytic conditions. An algebraic identity in a finite carrier need not extend continuously to a completion unless the multiplication and relevant domains are controlled.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A local algebraic quantum calculation does not provide renormalized Lorentzian products or a positive representation of the full theory. The result type and dependency tag must identify which algebra was actually constructed.

terms.label: Quotient
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: A quotient groups objects that a specified rule regards as equivalent and treats each group as one object. It removes distinctions that the rule says should not matter.
definitions.physics: A quotient removes declared redundancies or null directions. Observables, dynamics and pairings descend only when compatible with the equivalence relation.
definitions.mathematics: Given an equivalence relation, the quotient is the set of equivalence classes. Vector-space or algebra quotients require subspaces or ideals compatible with the relevant operations.
definitions.specialist: State the quotient relation and the structures proved to descend. Local functionals modulo boundary terms, gauge-state reduction and residual cohomology are different quotient constructions.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For gauge descriptions, this can organize different descriptions of the same proposed physical situation. But a quantity is well defined on the quotient only if equivalent descriptions give the same quantity.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Deleting an inconvenient mode is not automatically a valid physical quotient. The programme requires showing that the removed directions are actually redundant and that the intended physical structures survive the reduction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A quotient topology or descended pairing brings further conditions. Cohomology is a particular quotient of closed by exact elements, defined only when the differential-square condition places the image inside the kernel.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A certified class in one quotient is not automatically a physical state in another. The failed full export cannot authorize cohomological claims relying on its inconsistent differential, even if a formal quotient expression can be written.

terms.label: Kernel and image
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: The kernel of a linear map contains the inputs it sends to zero. Its image contains the outputs it can actually produce. These two collections reveal what the map loses and what it reaches.
definitions.physics: For a linear operator, the kernel solves the homogeneous equation and the image describes reachable sources or outputs. Both depend on the domain and boundary conditions.
definitions.mathematics: For T:V→W, ker T={v:T(v)=0} and im T={T(v):v∈V}. In a complex, d²=0 implies im d is contained in the next kernel.
definitions.specialist: Cocycle and trivialization calculations must use the actual operator and domain. An expected residual basis cannot be hard-coded as the kernel computation’s answer.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: If a map only reads one component of a vector, changes in the other components are invisible to it. Cohomology compares two related collections of this kind; “kernel” elsewhere can also mean an integral kernel, a different object.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Kernel vectors can represent solutions, redundancies or residual directions according to the operator. Their existence alone does not give a particle interpretation, and finite rank calculations need not settle infinite-dimensional range questions.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The algebraic image and its topological closure can differ. Reduced cohomology sometimes uses that closure, so the quotient convention must be specified rather than inferred from finite-dimensional intuition.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: This entry concerns null spaces and ranges, not the distributional kernel of a propagator. Preserve that distinction when connecting exact matrix certificates to analytic Green-operator claims.

terms.label: Cocycle and coboundary
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: A cocycle is an object that passes the complex’s consistency test. A coboundary is one produced by applying the differential to an earlier object, so it counts as trivial in cohomology.
definitions.physics: A cocycle is closed under the declared gauge or cohomological differential; a coboundary is exact. Their quotient can classify observables, deformations or anomalies, depending on the problem.
definitions.mathematics: For a differential d, a cocycle z satisfies dz=0 and a coboundary has the form db. Square-zero makes every coboundary closed, allowing the quotient H=ker d/im d.
definitions.specialist: Retain exact cocycle and trivialization witnesses together with the generated ansatz and canonical reduction. A basis printed by a producer is not an independent nontriviality check.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Every coboundary is a cocycle when the differential squares to zero. The interesting question is whether a given cocycle is also a coboundary; checking only that it passes the first test does not settle that.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A nonzero representative need not be a nontrivial class. One must check whether an allowed primitive removes it, with the correct degree, locality and boundary conventions.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Nontriviality requires ruling out b in the specified domain. A primitive outside the allowed local or regularity class does not establish triviality in the original problem.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Local BRST classes, integrated functionals modulo boundary terms and residual classes use different domains. A certificate in one must not be cited as the answer for another without a verified comparison.

terms.label: Chain map
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: A chain map connects two differential complexes while respecting their consistency operations. Applying the map and then the differential must agree with doing those steps in the reverse order.
definitions.physics: A chain map intertwines the differentials of two gauge or homological descriptions. It can support a reduction or transport of classes when the complexes are valid.
definitions.mathematics: A degree-zero map f between cochain complexes is a chain map when d_D f=f d_C. It then induces a map on cohomology.
definitions.specialist: The full-export chain-map identity must be checked directly for the supplied differential and projection or inclusion. Formal transport metadata cannot substitute for the coefficient identity.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: This is one precise meaning of two descriptions fitting together. It does not automatically say that lengths, probabilities or causal locations are preserved; those require additional checks.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Gauge compatibility, pairing preservation and causal support are distinct conditions. The current projection audit shows why a formal transport claim must be tested on the actual exported maps rather than assumed from their construction labels.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: It need not induce an isomorphism, preserve a pairing or have a continuous inverse. Those are additional assertions. If either advertised differential fails square-zero, the usual induced-cohomology interpretation is unavailable.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The trace/ghost candidate supplies selected repaired identities, but full nilpotency, chain-map and cyclic compatibility remain separate gates. A partial repair is not a certified full transfer.

terms.label: Homotopy contraction
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: A homotopy contraction relates a large complex to a smaller one while accounting for the information removed as trivial. It uses maps in both directions and an explicit correction describing their difference from doing nothing.
definitions.physics: A contraction packages projection, inclusion and a homotopy connecting their composite to the identity. It can organize transfer from a full gauge complex to residual data.
definitions.mathematics: In a common convention, maps p and i satisfy pi=1 and 1−ip=dh+hd, together with chain-map conditions and any stated side conditions. Sign conventions depend on grading.
definitions.specialist: Use pi_cl for the homological projection in the programme’s notation. Keep the imported operators and exact domains fixed when verifying contraction data.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: It is more than keeping a convenient subset of components. The maps must satisfy identities showing that the reduction respects the original consistency structure.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The algebraic identities do not by themselves preserve positivity, causal support or analytic domains. Those requirements must accompany any physical interpretation of the reduced model.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A homotopy equivalence supports a cohomology comparison when the complexes are valid. Checking selected contraction blocks does not establish every differential-square or pairing identity required for the full object.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The trace/ghost candidate’s repaired contraction identities do not certify full nilpotency, chain maps or cyclicity. The classical import gate remains closed until all required data pass their own checks.

terms.label: Projection
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: A projection selects a specified part of an object in a consistent way. Applying an ordinary projection twice has the same effect as applying it once.
definitions.physics: A projection can select a sector or participate in a reduction to residual data. Orthogonal, gauge and homological projections have different compatibility requirements.
definitions.mathematics: An endomorphism P is idempotent when P²=P. In a contraction, a map p:C→H is instead paired with an inclusion i:H→C satisfying pi=1; ip is the associated endomorphism.
definitions.specialist: Reserve pi_cl for homological projection and P for kinetic or witness operators. Inspect the actual projection and inclusion coefficients before asserting transport compatibility.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Which part is selected matters. Selecting coordinates can lose information needed for an equation, a pairing or a detector reading. A physically useful reduction must show that the relevant structures survive.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A projection formula is not automatically gauge-compatible or support-preserving. In the observable extension audit, a simple metric block can preserve compact support while a different required chain-map relation still fails.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Orthogonality additionally refers to an inner product. Neither idempotence nor a right-inverse identity alone gives a chain map or preservation of cohomological and analytic structures.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The full metric projection’s audited defect is substantive even though some order-zero source-lift identities hold. Preserve those separate results rather than treating one successful projection property as certification of all others.

terms.label: Cyclicity
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: Cyclicity is a compatibility rule saying that certain rearrangements inside a pairing give the same result, with the signs required by the kinds of objects involved.
definitions.physics: Cyclicity expresses compatibility of differentials or operations with the declared graded pairing. It is an additional condition in the classical reduction and quantum transfer programme.
definitions.mathematics: For a differential graded space, cyclic compatibility relates moving the differential or multilinear operations between paired arguments, with signs determined by degrees and pairing conventions.
definitions.specialist: Cyclicity is a required classical import check, independent of nilpotency, contraction and chain-map verification. Keep the pairing, suspension conventions and imported degrees explicit.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: It helps ensure that a reduction preserves more than its equations. A map may respect a differential while failing to respect the pairing that carries the model’s variational or interaction structure.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: It is not the same as time periodicity, a positive inner product or a trace identity quoted without grading conventions. Pairing and degree data must accompany the formula.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The exact identity depends on those conventions. A chain map preserves differentials but need not preserve the cyclic structure, so the two checks are logically distinct.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The current partial trace/ghost repair does not supply a complete cyclic transfer certificate. No residual quantum interpretation should inherit cyclicity merely because the relevant maps satisfy some unpaired identities.

terms.label: Exact arithmetic
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: Exact arithmetic keeps numbers such as fractions without rounding them to a limited number of decimal digits. This allows a finite identity to be checked as exactly zero rather than merely very small.
definitions.physics: Exact rational or algebraic arithmetic verifies finite coefficient identities without a numerical tolerance. Rational-complex coefficients have rational real and imaginary parts.
definitions.mathematics: Exact arithmetic uses a specified effective representation of numbers and operations, with exact equality where supported. Rational arithmetic is a basic case; algebraic extensions require their own canonical representations.
definitions.specialist: Canonical ranks, cocycle tests and trivialization witnesses must use exact arithmetic in this programme. Numerical agreement cannot certify those identities.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For example, one third plus two thirds is exactly one in rational arithmetic. A tiny floating-point residual is a different kind of evidence and can hide cancellation or precision problems.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: It is appropriate for the programme’s finite mode residuals and algebraic complex checks. It does not itself control infinite sums, convergence, measurement error or empirical accuracy.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A symbolic expression is not automatically reduced to a form with decidable equality. Record the coefficient domain, normalization and equality procedure behind rank or cocycle computations.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Conversely, an exact finite result cannot certify an infinite analytic theorem without its additional argument. Receipts must distinguish the arithmetic type and retain hashes of imported coefficients rather than silently regenerating a preferred answer.

terms.label: Finite field
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: A finite field is an algebraic number system with finitely many elements in which addition, multiplication and division by nonzero elements obey field rules. It is not a physical field with finitely many wave modes.
definitions.physics: A finite field is a coefficient-domain choice, not a mode cutoff or a finite spatial lattice. It changes arithmetic, including its characteristic.
definitions.mathematics: A finite field has order pⁿ for a prime p and positive integer n. In characteristic p, adding one to itself p times gives zero.
definitions.specialist: The atlas’s finite-field and finite-mode constructions are not equivalent merely because both admit finite computation. Preserve the scalar domain, carrier and obligation in comparisons.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Arithmetic modulo a prime gives a simple example. This dictionary separates the two meanings because “finite field” and “finite-mode field model” describe different mathematical choices.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A physical model using finitely many rational-complex coefficients still uses an infinite scalar field. Results obtained after reduction modulo a prime need a justified bridge before being used as claims about the original rational or real model.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Reduction modulo a prime can alter ranks or erase nonzero coefficients. The coefficient domain must remain part of any exact certificate; finite cardinality and finite-dimensionality are independent properties.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: An identity verified in a finite field is evidence in that field. It does not automatically prove the characteristic-zero identity or supply the continuum interpretation used by a wave or gravity theorem.

terms.label: Fourier mode
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: Fourier modes are simple oscillating patterns used as building blocks for more complicated signals or waves. Their coefficients tell us how much of each pattern is present.
definitions.physics: A Fourier expansion resolves data into oscillatory modes adapted to the domain and boundary conventions. The normalization determines coefficients, derivative weights and energy formulas.
definitions.mathematics: On a periodic domain, complex exponentials form the familiar Fourier family. Differentiation multiplies coefficients by frequency factors, with constants fixed by the period convention.
definitions.specialist: The finite chiral fixtures exploit finite sums and integer frequency weights in the chosen normalization. That explains their exact arithmetic without granting a general infinite expansion theorem.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A sound can be described by several frequencies. An individual oscillation usually extends across the whole domain, so retaining only finitely many frequencies does not automatically produce a spatially confined disturbance.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Finite mode calculations can be exact. An infinite expansion requires convergence in a declared topology, and its support or state interpretation cannot be inferred solely from the coefficient list.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Formal coefficient manipulations require analytic justification for infinite sums. Different convergence notions—pointwise, norm, distributional or smooth—support different subsequent operations.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Galerkin nesting, completed energy spaces and causal localization remain additional obligations. Do not identify finite support in Fourier coefficients with compact support in spacetime.

terms.label: Galerkin approximation
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: A Galerkin approximation searches for a solution inside a chosen finite space, often spanned by a few modes, and tests the equation against a corresponding finite set of probes.
definitions.physics: A Galerkin method projects or weakly tests an equation on a finite-dimensional trial space. Trial spaces, test spaces and projection choices determine the method.
definitions.mathematics: The finite problem enforces a residual condition against the selected test space. Convergence depends on consistency, approximation properties and estimates appropriate to the equation and topology.
definitions.specialist: The ladder certifies Galerkin nesting within its labelled finite chiral construction. Its stated exclusions include completion, spatial localization and causal support.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Adding more modes gives larger approximation spaces. If the spaces are nested, earlier possibilities remain available, but the solutions still need not converge or preserve every property of the full problem.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Nesting is a structural property of the sequence of spaces. Stability, convergence, constraint compatibility and local support require separate arguments, especially when a mode truncation is used in a gauge theory.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A sequence of nested subspaces need not come with compatible selected solutions or a controlled limit. Exact vanishing for particular fixtures establishes their identities, not a general Galerkin convergence theorem.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Preserve that finite scope. A theorem supplying uniform estimates or an extension to a completed carrier is an additional result, not an interpretation already contained in the nesting certificate.

terms.label: Bound and estimate
terms.scope: Mathematical structures, hypotheses and their role in the atlas.

definitions.general: A bound limits how large or small a specified quantity can be. An estimate gives a controlled comparison. We need to know what is bounded, under which conditions and with which constants.
definitions.physics: An analytic estimate controls quantities such as energy, response or truncation error. Its dependence on data, cutoff and background determines what physical conclusion it can support.
definitions.mathematics: An estimate states an inequality on a declared domain, including parameter dependence and constants. A logical upper bound instead proves an assertion from a specified principle; a lower bound derives a principle from the assertion.
definitions.specialist: State the controlled object, quantifiers and dependency tags before interpreting a bound. The wave reversal’s lower bound concerns named reconstruction, while the reduced cutoff result concerns full regularity of corrections.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A bound on detector error is not a bound on computing time. The project also uses “upper bound” for sufficient mathematical axioms, which is a different use from a numerical inequality.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A sufficient stability estimate can fail without disproving every stable construction. Keep uncertainty-weighted observational scores, analytic norms and logical strength bounds separate even when all are summarized numerically or by an ordering.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Uniformity and effective availability of constants can change the theorem. A bare existence assertion for an estimate does not necessarily supply the modulus needed by a reconstruction procedure.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Neither is a runtime theorem or an empirical accuracy estimate. A failed universal Euclidean estimate targets that sufficient route, not every possible realization of the proposed physics.

terms.label: Chirality
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Chirality distinguishes two directional or handed sectors of a construction. In the wave benchmark, the chiral data describe the two directions in which the selected wave profiles travel.
definitions.physics: For the benchmark, chiral components are the left- and right-moving data entering the fixed wave construction. Their domain, zero-mean conditions and detector coupling are specified separately.
definitions.mathematics: Chiral splitting denotes a declared decomposition into two sectors, not a universal operation on every carrier. In the scalar periodic wave model, characteristic translation gives the concrete split.
definitions.specialist: Keep the wave benchmark’s chiral data distinct from W₊²/W₋² labels for centered curvature deformation classes. Similar plus/minus notation does not provide an identification between these objects.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: This is a useful way to split a simple wave into pieces. In other physics settings, chirality has a different precise definition, so the word alone does not identify a particle’s spin or a gravity mode’s physical status.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: This use should not be identified automatically with spinor chirality, helicity or a self-dual curvature sector. The relevant field type and geometry determine which decomposition is meant.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The decomposition’s maps, periodicity and coefficient conditions belong to the statement. A finite labelled chiral family does not itself define an infinite completed space or prove support properties of its members.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The finite fixture’s exact residual and energy claims concern its declared sector and normalization. No particle interpretation or full metric BV propagation follows from calling it chiral.

terms.label: Finite propagation speed
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Finite propagation speed means that a disturbance cannot affect arbitrarily distant places immediately. Its response stays inside a region determined by the allowed travel speed and elapsed time.
definitions.physics: A finite-propagation theorem controls the support of solutions from localized data using the operator and causal geometry. The source, data class and time interval must be specified.
definitions.mathematics: The statement is a support inclusion, often bounding solution support by the causal development of initial or source support. It requires more than the algebraic equation Pu=f.
definitions.specialist: The finite chiral ladder explicitly separates exact wave residuals from causal support. Its finite arithmetic certificate does not discharge a finite-propagation theorem for the completed carrier.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: This is stronger than simply having a formula that solves an equation. A mode extending across all space is not a localized disturbance, so a finite list of modes does not by itself demonstrate how support travels.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Mode truncations can obscure or destroy exact localization. A scalar hyperbolic example does not automatically establish finite propagation for the full constrained metric complex or its proposed Green operator.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Energy estimates or domain-of-dependence arguments can establish it under suitable hypotheses. The theorem must retain the geometry, regularity and boundary conditions on which those arguments rely.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Likewise, the tested hyperbolic witnesses have limited architecture scope. A failed witness is not a universal absence of finite propagation, and a successful reduced example is not a full Lorentzian certificate.

terms.label: Boundary condition
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A boundary condition specifies how a field behaves at the edge of its domain. It helps determine which solutions an equation allows.
definitions.physics: Boundary conditions constrain fields, variations or fluxes at a physical, artificial or asymptotic boundary. They affect allowed modes, conserved quantities and operator domains.
definitions.mathematics: Boundary data select a domain for a differential operator or a trace condition for solutions. Different choices can produce different self-adjoint extensions, spectra and uniqueness properties.
definitions.specialist: Record boundary assumptions with the action, operator and import certificate. Local identities modulo boundary terms are not identities of pointwise densities or automatically boundary-compatible transfers.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A string fixed at both ends vibrates differently from one with a free end, even if the same local wave equation describes its interior. Conditions at infinity or periodic identifications play related roles in other models.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: They must be compatible with the intended gauge structure and variational principle. Choosing convenient mode conditions does not automatically preserve the full boundary data needed by a classical or quantum construction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Initial conditions and boundary conditions answer different parts of an evolution problem. Formal integration by parts only discards boundary terms when the chosen support or boundary assumptions justify doing so.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The periodic wave benchmark and a full metric theory with boundary have different obligations. No boundary construction should be inferred merely from the existence of its bulk complex or finite mode spectrum.

terms.label: Green operator and propagator
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A Green operator turns a source into a solution of a linear equation. “Propagator” is a related physics word whose exact meaning depends on whether it describes classical response, a commutator or a quantum correlation.
definitions.physics: For a linear field operator, advanced and retarded Green operators solve source equations with designated support. Quantum propagator conventions can instead involve time ordering and a choice of two-point structure.
definitions.mathematics: A Green operator is a map between specified source and solution spaces satisfying the required left/right inverse identities and support conditions. Its distributional kernel is one representation of that map.
definitions.specialist: A complete Lorentzian off-shell BV propagator for the full metric complex remains unestablished absent its certificate. Keep scalar witnesses and reduced kernels separate from that obligation.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: An inverse formula does not yet tell us where the response occurs. Causal support and suitable domains must be checked, and a response function is not automatically a state assigning physical probabilities.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: State which object is meant. A Euclidean inverse or reduced-mode kernel does not establish a full Lorentzian off-shell propagator compatible with all fields and gauge identities.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The kernel’s existence, continuity and singularity structure are analytic claims. A formal inverse in a mode basis is insufficient without convergence and the intended domain and boundary conditions.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The failed full-export consistency prerequisite blocks the advertised dependent transfer. Neither a formal causal expression nor a local algebraic quantum calculation supplies the missing compatible full operator.

terms.label: Retarded and advanced solutions
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A retarded solution responds only where a source can influence later events. An advanced solution uses the opposite temporal support direction and is a useful mathematical counterpart.
definitions.physics: Retarded and advanced Green operators impose future and past support, respectively, for compactly supported sources under the declared hypotheses. Their difference enters the classical causal response structure.
definitions.mathematics: Given a time-oriented spacetime, the support of a retarded response lies in the causal future of source support; the advanced version lies in its causal past. Operator identities and admissible spaces are additional requirements.
definitions.specialist: Separate advanced/retarded identities, causal pairing and the state-dependent symmetric part of a two-point distribution. Matching a commutator does not establish positivity or Hadamard compatibility for the full gauge complex.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: These labels describe support relative to the chosen time orientation. Writing either word next to an inverse does not prove the support restriction; it must hold for the actual sources and geometry in the theorem.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The sign convention for that difference should be fixed. It is not a positive quantum two-point function by itself, and specifying it does not choose a physical state.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Existence and uniqueness need hypotheses such as appropriate hyperbolicity and global geometry. A support inclusion alone does not supply all those analytic properties.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: No Lorentzian certificate follows from a Euclidean spectral inverse. The imported geometry, field operator, domains and chain compatibility must be present at the scope of the claim.

terms.label: Hyperbolicity
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Hyperbolicity describes mathematical features of an equation that support wave-like evolution and finite-speed influence under suitable conditions. Different kinds of hyperbolicity impose different requirements.
definitions.physics: A normally hyperbolic second-order operator has wave-type principal part, proportional to the inverse metric times the identity on field components. Strong hyperbolicity concerns well-controlled characteristic structure for evolution systems.
definitions.mathematics: Hyperbolicity is a property of a specified principal symbol or evolution formulation. It does not identify the full lower-order operator, its domain or the global spacetime assumptions.
definitions.specialist: The two programme no-go results exclude the 24-field scalar normally-hyperbolic witness and the fixed-temporal cyclic 46-parameter first-order family. Their scopes must remain explicit.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: The term is not a guarantee that every proposed field theory has a complete causal construction. Starting data, constraints, boundaries and the whole set of coupled variables still matter.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: For standard first-order formulations, real characteristic speeds alone are insufficient without appropriate uniform control. The exact formulation and coefficient regularity must accompany any well-posedness conclusion.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Normally hyperbolic scalar-like systems and strongly hyperbolic first-order systems are different classes. Converting between formulations requires checking the allowed variables, constraints and preservation of the intended solution problem.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: They do not refute the classical BRST complex, residual cohomology or every possible physical spectrum or causal formulation. A new architecture needs a new certificate rather than an inference from either excluded family.

terms.label: Gauge fixing and constraints
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Gauge fixing chooses representatives among descriptions intended to represent the same physical situation. Constraints restrict which data or configurations are admissible. The two operations are related but not identical.
definitions.physics: Gauge conditions address redundant descriptions; constraints encode relations that admissible data or solutions must satisfy. Their compatibility, propagation and possible residual gauge freedom depend on the formulation.
definitions.mathematics: Gauge fixing can be formulated as a slice, a choice of additional equations or an algebraic procedure on an extended complex. Constraints define a subspace or submanifold only under suitable assumptions.
definitions.specialist: Retain gauge conditions, constraint class and allowed field content in propagation certificates. Cyclicity or principal-symbol success in a selected ansatz is not certification of every gauge condition.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Removing a variable because it is inconvenient is not enough. One must show that the choice preserves the intended physical possibilities and that the remaining data still satisfy the relevant restrictions.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A gauge-fixed operator may be easier to invert, but that inverse must still fit the gauge complex. A discarded classical direction is not proven unphysical merely because one convenient gauge omits it.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Existence and uniqueness of representatives can fail globally. Quotienting, imposing equations and choosing coordinates are different mathematical operations and need explicit comparison maps.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The current full-export failure concerns actual differential identities; it cannot be excused by invoking gauge redundancy without a corrected, fully checked construction. Nonlinear and physical-state obligations remain distinct.

terms.label: Equation of motion
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: An equation of motion states which configurations or histories obey a model’s dynamics. It can describe a stationary field as well as literal motion.
definitions.physics: Equations of motion are dynamical conditions, often obtained as Euler–Lagrange equations. Gauge identities are relations among those equations, not additional independent motions.
definitions.mathematics: An equation of motion is a differential or variational relation on the chosen configuration space. Its order, domain and weak formulation determine what counts as a solution.
definitions.specialist: Keep equations, gauge generators and Noether identities distinct in the encoded complex. Their compatibility must be checked on the actual coefficients and grading.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: An action is one way to derive such equations. Finding an equation is only the start: initial data, boundaries and an allowed solution space are needed before asking whether it has a useful solution.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A configuration can solve the equations while failing global or boundary conditions. A linearized solution also need not extend to the interacting equations or define a positive quantum state.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Identities among equations can make the system constrained or redundant. A zero residual for a finite ansatz proves satisfaction in that declared setting, not existence or uniqueness for arbitrary data.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A classical equation residual is not a BV quantum master-equation test. Neither exact finite solutions nor local quantum identities supply the full Lorentzian state and renormalization constructions.

terms.label: Conformal symmetry
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A conformal transformation rescales the metric while preserving angles and, in the Lorentzian setting, the light-cone directions. Conformal symmetry says the relevant theory respects an allowed version of this transformation.
definitions.physics: Local Weyl transformations rescale the metric by a positive position-dependent factor, with suitable weights for other fields. Four-dimensional pure Weyl gravity has the corresponding classical conformal invariance.
definitions.mathematics: A conformal class identifies metrics related by positive scalar rescaling. Conformal covariance of an operator or tensor requires a precise transformation law, which may involve weights.
definitions.specialist: Conformal symmetry is a physical premise whose classical encoding is imported through the authoritative complex. Local quantum breakings must be classified and, where possible, canceled within the appropriate cohomological problem.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A rescaling can vary from point to point in a local conformal symmetry. This is not simply changing the numerical units in one formula; fields and the action must transform in the specified way.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The statement depends on dimension, action and boundary assumptions. Quantum preservation is a separate question; a classical symmetry does not itself rule out an anomaly or supply positive physical states.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Invariance of a functional is not identical to pointwise invariance of every tensor component. Boundary terms, densities and the chosen variational class must be tracked when deriving symmetry identities.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A trace-anomaly coefficient, a determinant and a BV master-equation breaking are distinct results. Their relationship must be proved, not inferred solely from the shared word conformal.

terms.label: Curvature and Weyl tensor
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Curvature measures how geometry differs from flat geometry. The Weyl tensor is a particular trace-free part of spacetime curvature, central to the action used in Weyl gravity.
definitions.physics: The Riemann curvature tensor decomposes into Ricci-dependent parts and the trace-free Weyl part in the relevant dimension. The pure-Weyl action uses a contraction quadratic in Weyl curvature.
definitions.mathematics: The Weyl tensor is the totally trace-free curvature component, obtained by subtracting the metric–Ricci contributions from the Riemann tensor. Its definition and possible vanishing depend on dimension.
definitions.specialist: The residual labels W₊² and W₋² refer to centered deformation/vertex classes in the certified programme. They must not be interpreted as one-particle graviton states.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Curvature has several components with different roles. Saying that a theory uses the Weyl tensor does not mean all its solutions or physical predictions have already been determined from that one geometrical ingredient.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Index placement affects conformal transformation formulas, and the four-dimensional action has its specific scaling property. Gauge reduction, boundary conditions and quantum interpretation remain additional requirements.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A tensor identity, its integrated quadratic functional and a cohomology class represented by that functional are different objects. An invariant notation does not identify their mathematical result types.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Curvature-based local classifications inform quantum ansätze, but coefficients, master-equation restoration and full Lorentzian constructions require their own scoped evidence. The dictionary does not promote those lifecycle states.

terms.label: Higher-derivative theory
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A higher-derivative theory uses equations involving more time or space derivatives than a familiar lower-order model. This can require additional starting information and introduce extra solution directions.
definitions.physics: Higher-derivative actions can produce higher-order equations and enlarged dynamical data. The relation between action derivative order, equation order and physical degrees of freedom depends on constraints and degeneracies.
definitions.mathematics: Increasing differential order changes the initial-data problem and associated operator analysis. A factorization of the linearized operator may reveal branches but does not settle nonlinear compatibility or the full constrained system.
definitions.specialist: The programme separates classical directions, gauge quotient, nonlinear continuation and quantum-state tests. An additional classical direction is not automatically a negative-probability particle.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Extra directions are a reason to investigate stability and interpretation, not a single automatic verdict. One must ask whether they are redundant, survive interactions and can support acceptable probabilities.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Pure Weyl gravity leads to fourth-order metric equations. General instability arguments have hypotheses; a specific model must be assessed with its gauge structure and admissible sector rather than by terminology alone.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Degenerate operators and gauge identities can reduce independent data. Analytic domains, boundary conditions and the chosen first-order reduction are part of any claimed equivalence of formulations.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The scoped propagation witnesses and reduced positivity obstruction address different architectures and carriers. Neither is a universal no-go for all higher-derivative theories, and a stable free block does not certify interactions.

terms.label: Nonlinear continuation
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Nonlinear continuation asks whether a small solution direction found in an approximation can be extended to a solution of the full equations. A first-order possibility can fail at the next order.
definitions.physics: A linearized solution can source higher-order equations whose solvability imposes additional conditions. Nonlinear continuation tests those conditions in the declared background and perturbative class.
definitions.mathematics: The continuation problem seeks a family solving the nonlinear equation with a specified initial tangent. At successive orders, obstruction classes or compatibility conditions may prevent solving the correction equations.
definitions.specialist: Keep nonlinear admissibility distinct from the centered residual deformation classification and one-particle interpretation. A surviving class must be matched to the precise deformation problem before it supports a continuation claim.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A tangent direction can point along an apparent path that later runs into a constraint. The project therefore checks this step separately from finding a linear mode or removing redundant descriptions.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A nontrivial linear gauge class is not enough. Even successful formal continuation through several orders does not establish convergence of the expansion or a physical quantum state.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Formal power-series solvability and existence of an actual analytic or smooth family are distinct. Regularity, gauge choices and boundary conditions are part of the relevant function-space theorem.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A finite perturbative certificate covers its declared order and ansatz. It cannot silently establish an all-order or convergent interacting construction, much less full Lorentzian quantum consistency.

terms.label: Indefinite inner product
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: An indefinite pairing can give either sign when an object is paired with itself. Unlike a positive inner product, it does not directly define an ordinary squared length or a probability.
definitions.physics: Indefinite inner-product formalisms allow negative-norm and possibly null directions in an enlarged description. Their physical treatment depends on constraints, gauge reduction and the observable representation.
definitions.mathematics: An indefinite Hermitian form lacks positive definiteness. It therefore does not induce a norm by taking the square root of the self-pairing, even when it is nondegenerate.
definitions.specialist: The full graded classical pairing and a physical positive-state inner product are distinct structures. Neither cyclicity nor nondegeneracy of the former certifies the latter.
