general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Such pairings can be useful in a redundant gauge description. A separate argument is needed to obtain the physical state space and show that its probability assignments are nonnegative.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Preservation of an indefinite form is not the same as unitary evolution on a positive Hilbert space. Positive energy and real frequencies are also separate properties.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A nonzero null vector need not lie in the radical of the form. Quotienting a null subspace requires the correct compatibility conditions; it is not automatic removal of every vector with zero self-pairing.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: In the reduced positivity analysis, changing the involution or discarding a branch changes the problem. The no-repair conclusion must retain those fixed conventions rather than being generalized to every indefinite formulation.

terms.label: Vacuum
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A vacuum is a chosen quantum state regarded as a reference with no excitations of the specified kind. It is not simply the absence of mathematical structure or all physical effects.
definitions.physics: A vacuum choice specifies a reference state, often selected by symmetries or a ground-state condition where available. Its correlations and particle interpretation depend on the representation.
definitions.mathematics: A vacuum is extra state data, not a property of an algebra alone. A ground-state or symmetry-invariance criterion can select one in some settings but requires explicit dynamics and hypotheses.
definitions.specialist: The reduced vacuum-cylinder reference is a specified model input with provenance and sign conventions. Its acceptance and possible repairs are scoped to that carrier.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: What counts as an excitation depends on the theory and reference setting. Curved or time-dependent spacetime may not supply one preferred vacuum for every observer or construction.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A mode prescription called a vacuum must still satisfy positivity and the required field, gauge and regularity conditions. Those conditions cannot be inferred from its name.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Hadamard short-distance behavior does not generally single out a unique state. The symmetric part of a two-point function can vary while preserving a fixed commutator and local singularity class.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The reconciled reduced-reference hash does not certify the entire transitive classical import or a full metric vacuum. The current full-export consistency failure remains a separate barrier to dependent state constructions.

terms.label: Two-point function
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A two-point function describes a correlation between two field measurements or insertions. It can reveal how a state relates observations at different places and times.
definitions.physics: A two-point distribution encodes the expectation of two field insertions in a specified state or candidate state. Its antisymmetric part is tied to the commutator, while its symmetric part carries additional state information.
definitions.mathematics: The object acts on pairs of test functions or on an appropriate product test space. A state construction requires positive-type conditions, the field relations and suitable continuity.
definitions.specialist: The reduced obstruction considers candidates with a fixed commutator and stated Hadamard wavefront control, and tests whether positivity can be repaired smoothly. It does not supply the full metric two-point construction.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For ideal quantum fields it may be a distribution rather than an ordinary function at two points, so one uses smeared measurements. An arbitrary correlation formula does not automatically define a valid state.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Positivity, field equations, regularity and gauge compatibility impose separate constraints. For Gaussian or quasifree constructions, two-point data can determine higher correlations under additional conventions; this is not true for every state.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Having the right antisymmetric part is insufficient. Products, restrictions and pullbacks of distributional kernels need their own analytic hypotheses; formal pointwise manipulations can fail.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The compact-source lift and failed projection identity remain separate findings. A support-preserving block does not resolve the full action-normalized all-energy commutator comparison.

terms.label: Hadamard state
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A Hadamard state is a quantum state with a prescribed short-distance correlation structure suited to the spacetime field problem. The condition controls how its idealized correlations become singular at very small separations.
definitions.physics: The Hadamard requirement fixes the local vacuum-like singularity class of two-point data for the declared linear field theory. It supports the definition of local renormalized quantities under the appropriate framework.
definitions.mathematics: The Hadamard condition has a microlocal formulation restricting the two-point distribution’s wavefront set to specified null-related covectors with an orientation condition. Its exact version depends on the field operator and conventions.
definitions.specialist: The reduced cutoff theorem fixes a reference singularity and commutator and excludes an admissible smooth positive repair on its full declared mode family. Its dependency is REDUCED-MODE.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: It does not mean the correlations are smooth everywhere. Nor does a candidate with the right singularity pattern automatically have nonnegative probabilities; without positivity, it has not yet earned the full state interpretation.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A positive state must also satisfy the field relations and normalization; gauge theories add compatibility requirements. Checking the singularity class alone does not construct a BRST-compatible physical state for the full metric complex.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Smooth changes do not alter that singularity structure, but they can affect positivity. A theorem about candidate distributions should not call them states before the positive-functional conditions have been established.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: This is not a theorem that the full metric BRST-compatible Hadamard state has been constructed, nor a universal obstruction for every changed carrier. The classical import and full observable comparison remain separate gates.

terms.label: Commutator and CCR
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: The commutator measures how much the order of two operations matters. CCR stands for Canonical Commutation Relations, the specified quantum relations between certain pairs of observables.
definitions.physics: For operators or algebra elements, the commutator is AB−BA. Canonical Commutation Relations (CCR) encode the chosen quantization of canonical or smeared field variables, with normalization and sign conventions fixed.
definitions.mathematics: Canonical Commutation Relations (CCR) are algebraic relations on generators, often expressed in a smeared or Weyl form to handle analytic issues. Unbounded operator products require compatible domains.
definitions.specialist: Canonical Commutation Relations (CCR) are held fixed in the reduced positivity repair problem. Dropping a branch, rescaling inconsistently or changing the involution alters the stated problem.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For ordinary numbers, reversing multiplication changes nothing; quantum observables can behave differently. Matching these relations is important, but it does not alone provide a state with sensible probabilities.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The antisymmetric part of two-point data is constrained by those relations. Positivity lies in an additional condition on the full state or covariance and can fail even when the commutator is correct.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A representation of the relations and a positive state on their algebra are further objects. A formal bracket identity alone does not certify their existence on the intended completed carrier.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The reconciled reduced reference passes its direct oscillator and CCR checks, but the full metric all-energy commutator transport remains unestablished. A direct reduced check cannot supply that missing full-complex interface.

terms.label: Regularization and renormalization
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Regularization introduces a controlled way to handle expressions that are otherwise singular or undefined. Renormalization specifies how to adjust or extend the calculation so that the intended quantities satisfy stated conditions.
definitions.physics: Regularization and renormalization are related but distinct steps. Renormalization can be formulated as choosing extensions of singular distributions or compatible local counterterms, without treating a regulator as a physical component.
definitions.mathematics: Renormalization may construct extensions of distributions from nonsingular configurations to coincident points, with controlled ambiguity. A formal subtraction algorithm and a theorem satisfying all required identities are different claims.
definitions.specialist: Classify counterterms and anomalies before coefficients, then test local QME restoration before residual transfer. Local algebraic renormalization data remain distinct from renormalized Lorentzian time-ordered products.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A temporary cutoff can be useful, but removing it is not simply erasing the cutoff symbol. One must show what remains well defined and which choices affect the final physical interpretation.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The allowed freedom is constrained by locality, symmetry and normalization conditions. A computed divergence or counterterm coefficient does not alone establish a restored quantum master equation or causal interacting theory.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Domains, scaling conditions and consistency under composition must be specified. In perturbation theory, the result can remain a formal series rather than a convergent nonperturbative object.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Neither a determinant nor a beta function certifies the latter. Keep LOCAL-ALGEBRAIC, EUCLIDEAN-SPECTRAL and LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL dependencies visible rather than letting the word renormalized promote the claim.

terms.label: Counterterm
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A counterterm is an allowed additional term used to adjust a quantum calculation while respecting specified rules. It can cancel a problematic contribution or implement a chosen normalization.
definitions.physics: Counterterms encode local renormalization freedom subject to dimensional, symmetry, grading and boundary restrictions. Which terms are allowed is a classification question separate from their coefficients.
definitions.mathematics: The counterterm space is an ansatz of allowed functionals modulo the declared equivalences. The relevant BRST differential and quotient by total derivatives or boundary terms must be fixed.
definitions.specialist: The programme requires counterterm and anomaly classification before coefficient computation. Restoring the local quantum master equation precedes any residual transfer of the correction.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: It is not permission to add anything that makes an answer look desirable. The available terms must first be classified, and the corrected result must then be checked against the relevant identities.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: A candidate counterterm can be admissible without its coefficient being known. A coefficient can be computed without proving that the complete local quantum identity has been restored.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A local density and its integrated functional need not have the same classification problem. Exact canonical reduction should retain witnesses rather than assuming a desired basis in advance.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: These LOCAL-ALGEBRAIC steps do not construct Lorentzian causal products or a physical state. Literature coefficients, spectral determinants and local BV breakings are distinct inputs requiring an explicit comparison if combined.

terms.label: Anomaly
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: An anomaly is a failure of a symmetry or consistency identity when a classical description is carried into the relevant quantum construction. The precise identity matters.
definitions.physics: An anomaly can refer to different quantum effects, including current or trace identities and BV master-equation breakings. These objects are related only through specified arguments, not by terminology alone.
definitions.mathematics: A local anomaly problem often imposes a consistency condition and identifies breakings modulo variations of allowed counterterms. The resulting cohomology depends on degree, locality and the quotient convention.
definitions.specialist: The programme separates CLASSIFIED, COEFFICIENT_COMPUTED and QME_RESTORED results. A local cancellation is a LOCAL-ALGEBRAIC conclusion, not a LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL construction.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Some apparent failures can be removed by an allowed adjustment; others represent an obstruction within the stated rules. The word anomaly should therefore name what failed and whether its removal has actually been shown.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Classifying a possible anomaly is not computing its coefficient. Computing a nonzero expression is not yet proving it is unremovable by an admissible local counterterm.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A cocycle can be trivial in one space but nontrivial in a restricted one. Keep pointwise densities, integrated functionals and residual classes separate when formulating the obstruction.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: A background trace anomaly or beta function must not be used as a BV breaking without its explicit identification. No residual or full quantum lifecycle state is promoted merely by publishing an anomaly explanation.

terms.label: Loop expansion
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A loop expansion organizes quantum corrections into successive orders. “One-loop” names one such order, not an assertion that the whole quantum problem has been solved.
definitions.physics: Loop order tracks powers of the quantum expansion parameter, conventionally ℏ, in perturbative contributions. Graph topology often records that order in a Feynman-diagram organization.
definitions.mathematics: The construction may be a formal power series with algebraic coefficient identities at each order. Existence of those coefficients does not imply convergence at a finite physical value of the parameter.
definitions.specialist: Record both loop order and lifecycle state. A one-loop classified breaking, computed coefficient, canceled local identity and transferred residual term are four different achievements.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: It resembles keeping a few stages of an approximation, although the expansion may be formal rather than convergent. A result at one order needs its order stated whenever it is used in a broader claim.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Field amplitude order and loop order are different. A one-loop coefficient can be useful without establishing higher-order consistency, a nonperturbative state or renormalized Lorentzian products for the full theory.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Recursive restoration can encounter new obstructions at later orders. The algebra, regularization conventions and allowed counterterms must be part of the statement at every step.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Do not infer all-order QME restoration or Lorentzian certification from a finite-order LOCAL-ALGEBRAIC or EUCLIDEAN-SPECTRAL calculation. The source operator and conventions must remain compatible with the classical import.

terms.label: Time-ordered product
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A time-ordered product organizes field insertions according to their temporal order. It is used in perturbative descriptions of interactions and responses.
definitions.physics: Time-ordered products extend the products used in perturbative interactions while obeying causal factorization and other required normalization conditions. Gauge compatibility adds further identities.
definitions.mathematics: Singular distributional products need controlled extensions at coincident configurations. The extensions must form a compatible family satisfying locality, symmetry and causal requirements in the chosen framework.
definitions.specialist: Renormalized Lorentzian time-ordered products for the full metric BV complex remain unestablished absent an explicit certificate. They belong to a LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL construction.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: For ideal fields, bringing insertion points together can create singularities. Defining the product there is part of the mathematical construction; an informal ordering symbol does not supply the missing definition.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: In a Lorentzian theory, their construction is distinct from a Euclidean determinant or a free two-point function. A candidate propagator is an ingredient, not a certificate for all renormalized products.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Different allowed extensions encode renormalization freedom. Their existence as formal perturbative data is separate from convergence of an interacting theory or existence of a positive full state.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Local anomaly classification or QME restoration does not by itself supply these products. Nor does the reduced Hadamard reference repair the full-export consistency prerequisite on which the advertised transfer depended.

terms.label: Algebraic quantum field theory
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: AQFT stands for Algebraic Quantum Field Theory. It starts with algebras of observables associated with regions of spacetime and asks how those algebras relate. States then supply expectation values and probabilities.
definitions.physics: Algebraic Quantum Field Theory (AQFT) organizes observables, locality and dynamics through algebraic relations. Its perturbative variant, pAQFT, constructs interacting observables as formal perturbative objects under specified hypotheses.
definitions.mathematics: Algebraic Quantum Field Theory (AQFT) assigns compatible observable algebras to spacetime regions, with axioms expressing properties such as isotony and causal compatibility. States are positive normalized functionals in the relevant setting.
definitions.specialist: Algebraic Quantum Field Theory (AQFT), including perturbative AQFT, names a target framework rather than a completed result of this programme. A causal perturbative construction for the full metric complex remains uncertified.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: This keeps the rules for observables distinct from a particular state-vector description. The perturbative form, pAQFT, develops interactions order by order and still needs precise causal and renormalization conditions.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: An algebraic formulation does not remove the state problem. The relevant positive representations, singularity control and gauge consistency must still be established for the model under study.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The precise category and axioms vary by formulation. A locally covariant or perturbative construction is an additional specification, not something automatically attached to any algebra of finite matrices.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Local BV calculations and reduced-mode state tests contribute separately scoped evidence. They cannot certify full Lorentzian causal products, compatible states or the quantum master equation by adopting the AQFT label.

terms.label: Scattering
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: Scattering studies how an interaction changes incoming disturbances or particles into outgoing ones. It provides one route from a theory to quantities that can be compared with experiments.
definitions.physics: A scattering construction compares suitable asymptotic dynamics and states, often through an S-matrix. Its existence, normalization and unitarity depend on the model and physical setting.
definitions.mathematics: Wave operators or other asymptotic constructions relate interacting dynamics to a reference evolution under stated convergence conditions. The resulting scattering map requires appropriate domains and state spaces.
definitions.specialist: A residual vertex class classifies an interaction direction; it is not automatically an S-matrix element or a one-particle state. The physical representation and causal interacting construction remain separate obligations.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: That route assumes the model has meaningful incoming and outgoing states. A formal interaction term alone does not show that such states exist or that their predicted probabilities are sensible.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Not every spacetime or interacting theory admits the same asymptotic description. A local vertex or free propagator does not establish a complete scattering theory, and comparison with data adds operational assumptions.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Formal perturbative amplitudes are distinct from an operator theorem about asymptotic completeness or unitary scattering. The relevant limiting argument cannot be inferred from a finite list of coefficients.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: No full metric Lorentzian scattering certificate follows from the current local or reduced results. Retain that boundary when placing an amplitude calculation in a theory journey.

terms.label: Empirical prediction and fit
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A prediction states what a model expects a specified observation to show. A fit chooses model parameters using data. A good fit and a successful new prediction provide different kinds of evidence.
definitions.physics: Empirical comparison connects a mathematical observable to calibrated measurements and an error model. Fitting estimates parameters under that protocol; predictive validation tests the resulting model on the stated task or data.
definitions.mathematics: A fit solves a specified estimation or optimization problem, with loss function, parameter domain and data treatment fixed. Identifiability and uncertainty require additional analysis.
definitions.specialist: Keep empirical score, acceptance gate and physical interpretation distinct. Record dataset version, weights, nuisance parameters and allowed flexibility before claiming comparative success.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A flexible curve can match known points without correctly describing the mechanism behind them. The dataset, parameter freedom, uncertainty model and comparison rule are part of judging what the agreement means.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Unweighted and uncertainty-weighted scores can rank models differently. A bounded comparison does not establish universal empirical superiority or validate every theoretical component of the model.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: A small residual norm is a property of that objective on that dataset. It does not itself prove uniqueness of parameters, statistical adequacy or equivalence of the fitted models’ mechanisms.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The galaxy case studies address bounded protocols, not blanket validation of Weyl gravity or another programme. Exact mathematical certificates do not substitute for the observational assumptions entering those tests.

terms.label: Residual and uncertainty weighting
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: An observational residual is the difference between a predicted value and a measured value, using a stated sign convention. Uncertainty weighting changes how strongly each discrepancy contributes to a comparison.
definitions.physics: Weighted residual analysis accounts for a declared noise model. Independent Gaussian errors motivate a sum of squared discrepancies divided by variances; correlated errors require the covariance structure.
definitions.mathematics: For residual vector r and a suitable nonsingular covariance matrix C, the quadratic statistic rᵀC⁻¹r measures discrepancies in the covariance geometry. Its distributional interpretation needs statistical assumptions.
definitions.specialist: Keep data provenance, sign convention, covariance, fitted parameters and acceptance threshold with the empirical receipt. Do not substitute an unweighted curve comparison for the stated weighted protocol.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: A small error on a very precise measurement can matter more than a larger error on a noisy one. This use of residual has nothing to do with the residual complex in the project’s homological calculations.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The weights must be justified and parameter fitting accounted for. A model can improve an unweighted score while failing an uncertainty-weighted gate, without either score alone identifying the correct physical mechanism.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Changing C changes the objective and its geometry. This is not cohomological reduction, and a positive quadratic statistic does not imply positivity of a quantum state.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The homological residual sector is a different result kind. Automatic annotation of bare residual is avoided so that an empirical discrepancy cannot accidentally inherit the meaning of a reduced cohomology class.

terms.label: Galaxy rotation curve
terms.scope: Physical meaning, analytic conditions and limits of interpretation.

definitions.general: A galaxy rotation curve describes how orbital speed varies with distance from a galaxy’s center. It is used to compare gravitational models with inferred motion in galaxies.
definitions.physics: Rotation-curve modeling connects a gravitational potential and matter model to inferred circular velocities under the declared geometry and dynamical assumptions. Systematic and measurement uncertainties affect the test.
definitions.mathematics: The comparison is an inverse or estimation problem: model parameters determine a velocity profile, and data constrain them through a chosen loss and uncertainty model.
definitions.specialist: Retain the dataset, radial selection, normalization, mass-model freedom and weighting in the empirical claim. The relevant evidence is protocol-specific rather than a universal theorem about galactic dynamics.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: The curve is not a direct reading of the gravity equation alone. Distances, viewing angle, visible matter and measurement errors enter its interpretation, so a model comparison needs those choices stated.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The project’s conformal-gravity comparisons use bounded datasets and protocols. A successful or failed fit there should not be generalized to every galaxy or every realization of the theory.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Parameter degeneracies, nuisance inputs and correlations can change what is identifiable. Minimizing one residual measure is not equivalent to passing every statistical acceptance criterion.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: These tests neither certify nor refute the full quantum construction. A theory journey must connect the particular classical prediction to its operational and observational inputs without importing unrelated certificate strength.

terms.label: Formal proof and computational check
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s constructions, dependencies and current status.

definitions.general: A formal proof gives a derivation in explicit rules that a proof system can check. A computational check runs a specified test on encoded data. Both can be valuable, but they answer the question they were actually given.
definitions.physics: A computational certificate can verify exact algebra, numerical behavior or a finite witness. A formal proof checks a derivation relative to a formal statement and trusted logical environment.
definitions.mathematics: Formalization specifies the language, axioms, definitions and derivation of the claimed statement. A program test can instead establish a finite predicate on inputs without encoding the surrounding infinite theorem.
definitions.specialist: Receipts distinguish written proof, exact witness verification, numerical diagnostics, reproduction and independent checking. Do not promote one evidence type by changing its description.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Checking many finite examples is not a proof about all infinite cases. A checked derivation also does not decide whether its assumptions describe nature or whether the explanation accurately states its theorem.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Neither independently validates the physical modeling assumptions. The project’s wave reversal combines a written infinite argument with finite exact checks; it is not presented as a completed proof-assistant derivation.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The link between mathematical objects and their machine representations is a separate correctness obligation. Independent verification should expose which decisive assumptions are shared with the producer.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The wave theorem’s infinite argument remains unformalized in a proof assistant, and the full classical import is not certified by partial matrix checks. A timeout or skip is never a passing proof obligation.

terms.label: Fixed wave-detector benchmark
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s constructions, dependencies and current status.

definitions.general: The fixed wave-detector benchmark holds the wave setup and detector rule steady while changing the information supplied about approximations. This isolates the reason one reconstruction task is harder than another.
definitions.physics: The benchmark uses declared periodic chiral data and a fixed smeared detector. The supplied-rate and rate-free inputs are compared with the same intended observable and output representation.
definitions.mathematics: The input consists of coded approximants with stated bounds and Cauchy conditions; the output is a fast name for a fixed scalar functional. Adding a modulus changes the information available in that input.
definitions.specialist: The benchmark realizes a standard scalar completeness reversal within the project’s specified observable. Its mathematical dependency tags are LOCAL-ALGEBRAIC and REDUCED-MODE.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: An error schedule tells us when an approximation is accurate enough. A bare promise of eventual agreement does not. Since the apparatus stays fixed, the comparison is not explained by switching to a more complicated detector.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The necessity argument already works at a fixed time and profile. Its extra logical requirement is amplitude completion, not a change in propagation or an added interaction.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The physical profile and detector are not varied to manufacture the lower bound. The reduction encodes an arbitrary scalar completion problem within those fixed ingredients.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Do not infer a uniform higher-type solver, a full field algebra or a metric BV state. Finite witness certificates support the encoding, while the infinite equivalence over RCA₀ remains a written argument.

terms.label: Finite chiral fixture
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s constructions, dependencies and current status.

definitions.general: A finite chiral fixture is one explicitly specified finite collection of wave modes and coefficients used for a controlled test. “Fixture” means the exact test object, not the whole continuum theory.
definitions.physics: The ladder starts from a labelled finite family of rational-complex chiral modes in the declared normalization. Integer differentiation weights and decidable rational equality support exact residual and energy checks.
definitions.mathematics: A fixture fixes its finite labels, coefficients and operations before the identity checks. Rational-complex means rational real and imaginary parts, not a finite scalar field.
definitions.specialist: Retain the exact fixture, arithmetic domain and quantifiers when citing the ladder’s initial rung. Its dependency is a finite algebraic construction, not a complete physical-state realization.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Its finite sums can be checked without rounding. Solving its wave equation and obtaining positive finite energy still does not say that it is spatially localized or that every infinite extension works.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: PRA is the stated base for each fixed fixture. Completion, causal support and spatial localization are explicitly additional obligations, not consequences of having finitely many modes.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: The certificate includes finite wave residuals, nesting and positive finite energy under the declared assumptions. A family of such checks must not be silently identified with a uniform infinite reconstruction theorem.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Nested Galerkin spaces do not certify a completed carrier or support-preserving propagation. Those transitions require their own representations, topology and independent interface checks.

terms.label: Completion ladder
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s constructions, dependencies and current status.

definitions.general: The completion ladder organizes successive requirements beyond a finite wave calculation: limits, suitable function spaces, distributions, energy control and support properties. Each step asks what extra information or assumptions are needed.
definitions.physics: The ladder compares declared carriers and representations for the wave problem, beginning with exact finite modes and proceeding toward analytic and energy constructions. Different rungs discharge different properties.
definitions.mathematics: Each rung specifies an object, base, added assumptions, established statements and exclusions. The transitions can change topology, coding, quantifiers or test class, not merely increase dimension.
definitions.specialist: The ladder is a typed evidence interface for scoped constructions. The finite PRA fixture and the RCA₀/ACA₀ reconstruction comparison must retain their distinct formulations.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: It is a map of obligations, not a promise that every higher step has been completed. A result at one rung should be read with its explicit additions and exclusions.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: Positive finite energy, completion and causal support are separate claims. A formal similarity of equations does not provide the maps or estimates needed to connect their carriers.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: Read the displayed arrows as claims requiring evidence, rather than inferring implications from their visual order. Representation invariance itself is an additional theorem with preservation conditions.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: Nothing in the ladder certifies the full metric BV propagator or a complete Lorentzian quantum theory. Its role is to expose missing joins and localize additional requirements in a controlled wave setting.

terms.label: Representation invariance
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s constructions, dependencies and current status.

definitions.general: Representation invariance asks whether a claim remains valid when the same intended object is described in another form. The change must preserve what the object means and what the task asks us to recover.
definitions.physics: A representation comparison needs explicit translations preserving the intended observable and relevant physical structure. Equality of informal interpretation is not enough to preserve computational or logical resources.
definitions.mathematics: Representations assign objects to names. An invariance theorem must specify translations between names and the resources under which those translations and their preservation properties exist.
definitions.specialist: Record the exact observable identification, input promises and translation assumptions in a representation comparison. Do not infer invariance from a shared physical label or matching finite examples.

general.heading: Example and distinction
general.text: Two descriptions can hide different amounts of information. If one includes an error schedule and the other does not, calling them “the same wave” does not make their reconstruction tasks identical.

physics.heading: Use in the model
physics.text: The WR/WRμ example deliberately changes convergence information. Any proposed invariant reformulation must state whether the translation supplies that information or changes the output guarantee.

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences
mathematics.text: An abstract carrier isomorphism need not be computable, continuous or available in the weak base. These are separate questions, and the chosen output representation can also change the assertion.

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary
specialist.text: The wave reversal locates a genuine distinction between its declared codings; it does not prove that every possible representation has the same logical strength or that no alternative carrier can avoid the requirement.

terms.label: BRST formalism
terms.scope: How to read the programme’s constructions, dependencies and current status.

definitions.general: BRST stands for Becchi–Rouet–Stora–Tyutin. The formalism adds graded bookkeeping variables called ghosts to organize gauge redundancy through an operation that is required to square to zero.
definitions.physics: Becchi–Rouet–Stora–Tyutin (BRST) methods encode gauge structure using a graded differential. Depending on the gauge algebra and formulation, closure and the required field content need explicit treatment.
definitions.mathematics: Becchi–Rouet–Stora–Tyutin (BRST) structure is expressed by a degree-one differential on a graded space or algebra. The square-zero identity makes closed elements modulo exact ones meaningful.
definitions.specialist: Becchi–Rouet–Stora–Tyutin (BRST) identities must be checked on the actual imported operator. A formal expression bearing the name does not certify the current serialized full complex.

general.heading: Example and distinction

definitions.general: BV stands for Batalin–Vilkovisky. It is a way to organize a gauge theory’s fields, ghosts and additional variables called antifields so that their consistency is expressed by a master equation.
definitions.physics: The Batalin–Vilkovisky (BV) formalism extends the field space and uses an odd bracket to encode gauge structure and variational consistency. The master equation is central to the associated differential.
definitions.mathematics: Batalin–Vilkovisky (BV) data include graded variables, an odd bracket and an action satisfying the classical master identity in the stated setting. The induced differential organizes the corresponding cohomological problem.
definitions.specialist: Batalin–Vilkovisky (BV) data for quantum work must come from the authoritative classical import. Do not reconstruct a competing complex or infer a complete freeze from a partial snapshot.

general.heading: Example and distinction

physics.heading: Use in the model

definitions.physics: The Quantum Master Equation (QME) expresses compatibility of the quantum construction with the BV gauge structure under the chosen renormalization conventions. Possible breakings and counterterms must be analyzed in the correct local problem.
definitions.mathematics: The Quantum Master Equation (QME) is a specified identity on quantum action or observable data in the BV formalism. Its exact form depends on bracket, measure or renormalized-operator conventions.
definitions.specialist: Quantum Master Equation (QME) progress must distinguish CLASSIFIED, COEFFICIENT_COMPUTED, QME_RESTORED and RESIDUAL_TRANSFERRED. Local restoration is a LOCAL-ALGEBRAIC result unless stronger dependencies are independently certified.

definitions.mathematics: A residual complex is a target of a specified reduction with its own differential and structure. Its differential may vanish in a particular model, but that is a property to establish, not part of the general definition.
definitions.specialist: Keep certified W₊²/W₋² centered deformation classes distinct from the reduced reference’s state/cohomology representatives. They answer different questions and use different carriers.

terms.label: Dependency tag

definitions.general: A dependency tag identifies the kind of construction a result uses. It helps a reader tell an algebraic calculation, a Euclidean spectral calculation, a reduced mode result and a Lorentzian causal construction apart.
definitions.physics: The four programme tags are LOCAL-ALGEBRAIC, EUCLIDEAN-SPECTRAL, REDUCED-MODE and LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL. They type dependencies so a result from one setting is not silently used as a theorem in another.
definitions.mathematics: A dependency tag is metadata about a scoped construction, not a logical implication between categories. The underlying objects, maps and hypotheses remain the mathematical content.
definitions.specialist: Do not use REDUCED-MODE or EUCLIDEAN-SPECTRAL evidence to certify a LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL claim. LOCAL-ALGEBRAIC QME restoration likewise does not provide renormalized causal products.

general.heading: Example and distinction

physics.heading: Use in the model

mathematics.heading: Conditions and consequences

specialist.heading: Project role and claim boundary

definitions.specialist: Use LOCAL-ALGEBRAIC for the relevant local result kind and record its lifecycle separately. CLASSIFIED, COEFFICIENT_COMPUTED and QME_RESTORED are not interchangeable labels.

physics.heading: Use in the model
